guide.title: About 3G2 files
guide.markdown:
### What is a 3G2 file?

3G2 is a video container defined by 3GPP2, the standards group behind CDMA mobile networks, for clips shot and sent on phones. It uses the ISO media file format family as its foundation, and RFC 4393 registered its media types in March 2006. The preferred extension is .3g2, and .3gpp2 is also recognized.

A 3G2 can carry sound, moving pictures and timed text. The type video/3gpp2 is valid even when the file holds only audio, while audio/3gpp2 is reserved for files with nothing visual, and timed text counts as visual content. So a 3G2 that plays without a picture is not always broken.

You meet these files on older CDMA phones and in their MMS video. The format keeps files small, and its video is H.264 or MPEG-4. Recognizing the container does not guarantee that a player has a decoder for the video or sound inside it, which is the usual reason a 3G2 opens on one device and not on another.

### Programs that open 3G2 files

VLC media player and QuickTime Player both open 3G2 clips. These programs also handle the format:

**Windows, Mac and Linux**

- FFmpeg: registers .3g2 with its QuickTime and ISO base media demuxer.
- ffplay: the FFmpeg player, which uses the FFmpeg demuxers and decoders.

**Windows and Mac**

- Adobe After Effects: recognizes .3g2 as an import extension.

### 3G2 and MP4 compared

- **Extensions and media types**: .3g2 or .3gpp2 with video/3gpp2, where audio/3gpp2 is kept for files with nothing visual; .mp4 for MPEG-4 Part 14.
- **Standards**: 3G2 comes from 3GPP2 and is based on the MPEG-4 container. MP4 is defined in ISO/IEC 14496-14.
- **Video codecs**: a 3G2 holds H.264 or MPEG-4 video. MP4 takes H.264, H.265 and AV1.
- **Extras**: MP4 can carry subtitles and chapters.
- **Reach**: MP4 plays on nearly every device. The older 3G2 is kept small and was made for phones.

What this page does is decode the clip and write a new MP4. The picture is re-encoded by x264 using CRF 32 and its ultrafast preset, while the soundtrack is re-encoded as 96 kbps AAC. An oversized picture is scaled down to 1920 pixels along its longer edge, and playback speed tops out at 30 frames per second. Your 3G2 itself is never changed; you download a new file next to it.

Conversion happens in your browser, one clip at a time, with no file-size cap from the page. Pick several files and they queue, each saved under its own name with the .mp4 ending. No stream-selection options are passed, which leaves FFmpeg's defaults to pick the streams that reach the MP4. An audio-only 3G2 gives an MP4 with sound and no picture.

### Other ways to convert 3G2 to MP4

- **FFmpeg with a re-encode:** on Windows, Mac or Linux, run `ffmpeg -i handset.3g2 -c:v libx264 -c:a aac handset-share.mp4`. It encodes video with libx264 and audio with aac, and the result is lossy.
- **FFmpeg, copy the streams:** run `ffmpeg -i archive-phone.3g2 -c copy archive-phone.mp4`. Nothing is re-encoded, but it works only when MP4 accepts the streams inside.
- **Prism (Windows):** click Add File(s), set Output Format to MP4, check Encoder Options, pick a folder under Save to Folder and click Convert. NCH lists 3G2 input for Windows only.

### Problems with 3G2 files

- **No picture**: a video/3gpp2 file may be audio only, so a missing picture is not always a playback failure.
- **Won't play on a phone or in an editor**: the app in question may not have a decoder for the picture or sound stored in the file. Converting here writes new H.264 and AAC streams, provided FFmpeg can decode the original.
- **Corrupt after a transfer**: a text-style transfer that changes line endings or strips high bits can corrupt this binary format.
- **A damaged or cut-short clip**: a clip like this usually still converts, giving a shorter MP4, so compare the running time with the original.
- **A soft or blocky result**: encoding uses CRF 32 with the ultrafast preset and offers no quality control, so the MP4 can look worse than the 3G2.
- **An odd .3gpp2 ending**: it is the second registered extension for the same format. Rename it to .3g2 if a program only looks for that one.

guide.title: About 3GP and MOV
guide.markdown:
### What is a 3GP file?

The 3GP format comes from 3GPP, a specialization of ISO's media file layout, for messaging, downloads and packet-switched streaming on phones. A clip can combine video, speech, other sound and timed text. Video may be H.263, MPEG-4 Visual, AVC or HEVC, and sound may be an AMR variant or AAC. The extension doesn't tell you which a given clip uses, and a conforming parser may ignore boxes or codecs outside the spec. The media types are video/3gpp, and audio/3gpp for sound only.

A MOV is QuickTime's own container. It keeps video, audio, text and timecode in separate tracks and can hold many codecs, ProRes among them. Changing the ending doesn't transcode anything or install a missing decoder, which is why a real conversion is the safer route when an editor refuses the clip.

### Programs that open 3GP files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** VLC lists 3GP among its inputs, and FFmpeg reads 3GP containers. For the finished MOV, mpv plays it on the desktop.

### 3GP and MOV compared

- **Purpose**: 3GP was built for small phone clips. MOV is a general container used in editing.
- **Lineage**: 3GP is a simplified version of the MP4 container. MOV, the QuickTime container, is what MPEG-4's file format grew from.
- **Codecs**: a 3GP can carry H.263 and AMR audio. This converter writes H.264 and AAC.
- **Size**: the output keeps the frame size up to 1920 pixels and the frame rate up to 30 fps.

### Other ways to convert 3GP to MOV

- **FFmpeg transcode:** run `ffmpeg -i handset.3gp -c:v libx264 -c:a aac editable.mov` for new H.264 and AAC streams.
- **FFmpeg remux:** run `ffmpeg -i handset.3gp -c copy rewrapped.mov` to rewrap the streams without re-encoding. It works only if the original codecs fit MOV and your editor.

### Problems with 3GP files

- **No video in the file**: a 3GP may be sound only, and there is nothing to recover.
- **The editor rejects the MOV**: QuickTime containers can use codecs your editor lacks. Convert it, so the streams are H.264 and AAC.
- **Renamed file won't open**: the old codecs are still inside. Convert instead of renaming.
- **A MOV that stopped mid-write**: an ordinary MOV can be left unusable by a write that was cut short.

guide.title: About AAC files
guide.markdown:
### What is an AAC file?

AAC is a lossy audio codec developed by MPEG as MP3's successor; the name stands for Advanced Audio Coding. It is defined in MPEG-2 Part 7 and again in MPEG-4 Part 3. For a given bitrate it tends to sound better than MP3, so streaming, music downloads and phones lean on it.

The codec and the file are two things. AAC audio can sit inside an MP4 or QuickTime wrapper, which is what an .m4a file is. A standalone .aac file is different: it commonly carries ADTS framing, with no track information around it. The registered audio/aac media type covers that stream form, along with LATM/LOAS framing. Profiles such as LC, HE-AAC and HE-AAC v2 describe how the audio was coded, and a player has to support the profile as well as read the file.

A raw .aac stream can also start or end with ID3v1, ID3v2 or APE tags, which FFmpeg's aac demuxer reads along with the ADTS frames. The ADTS frame header holds a version bit that marks the stream as MPEG-2 or MPEG-4 AAC; FFmpeg's adts muxer writes 0, meaning MPEG-4, unless told otherwise. That bit is one reason a decoder built for one flavor can stumble on the other.

Because the same codec can live in either wrapper, moving between them is mostly a question of packaging.

### Programs that open AAC files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** VLC media player takes raw AAC as input and decodes the MPEG-4 version of AAC.
- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** FFmpeg includes an AAC decoder and its own AAC encoder.
- **Windows and Mac:** Adobe Audition imports AAC, including HE-AAC.

### AAC and MP4 compared

- **Extensions and media types**: .aac and audio/aac for a raw stream; .mp4 and video/mp4 for the container. Audio-only MPEG-4 files often use .m4a and the audio/mp4 type.
- **What each is**: AAC compresses sound. MP4, defined in ISO/IEC 14496-14 and first published in 2003, holds sound, video, subtitles and metadata in separate tracks.
- **Wrapper**: a raw .aac stream has none. Under the hood the container is ISO base media, an offshoot of QuickTime, and its track and timing data sit in nested boxes.
- **Video**: MP4 mostly holds H.264 video together with AAC audio, and other codecs, among them AV1, VP9, MP3 and Opus, can be stored in it as well. It does not need any video.

The wrapper changes, and so does the audio. On the page, FFmpeg decodes the AAC and encodes it again as AAC at 96 kbps inside an MP4. FFmpeg then makes a second pass that relocates the moov atom, its name for the index, to the front so players find the track information without reading the whole file. No picture is added, so you get an MP4 with sound only. The conversion runs entirely in your browser, so the recording is not uploaded anywhere, and each file in a batch becomes its own MP4.

### Other ways to convert AAC to MP4

Both methods copy the frames instead of encoding them again.

- **FFmpeg:** run `ffmpeg -i voice.aac -c:a copy voice-container.mp4`. Its documentation describes stream copy as no decoding or encoding, and its aac demuxer reads ADTS AAC, with any ID3v1/2 or APE tags in it. Nothing is re-encoded, so the audio keeps the bitrate it already had.
- **Bento4:** run `mp4mux --track aac:voice.aac voice-muxed.mp4`. Its documentation lists AAC input as ADTS format, and says that when you give no type before the colon, the type is inferred from the file extension. The output is the last name on the command line.

### Problems with AAC files

- **A file plays in one program and not another**: some decoders are built for MPEG-2 AAC only and cannot read the MPEG-4 variants. VLC accepts raw AAC input, so open the file there.
- **Renaming to .m4a did not help**: a new extension leaves the ADTS framing where it was and adds no MP4 wrapper. Only a real conversion changes the container.
- **The file is much larger once decoded**: AAC stores compressed audio, so an editor that unpacks it to raw samples uses far more space.
- **A ZIP does not shrink it**: AAC streams are already compressed, and zipping them usually saves little.

faqs.answer: Each page renders at up to twice its size. The limit applies to the whole page area, about 16.8 megapixels, so a big poster is scaled down and ends up smaller than twice its size. The JPEG is saved at quality 0.9.

faqs.question: Can I convert just one page of the file?
faqs.answer: No. The page converts every page it finds and gives each its own JPEG. Keep the one you want and delete the rest.

faqs.question: Can I drop in a whole folder of AI files?
faqs.answer: Choose them together and the page converts them one after another. Each result downloads as its own file, so expect one download for every picture, not a ZIP archive.

faqs.question: Is a JPEG a good copy of a logo?
faqs.answer: It works for a proof, a slide or a web page. It is a fixed set of pixels, so enlarging it later softens the edges, and it keeps no paths or live text. Keep the AI file as the master.

faqs.question: Which programs open an AI file?
faqs.answer: Adobe Illustrator opens it with every editable object. Inkscape can import AI artwork, and ImageMagick can read it, though neither gives Illustrator's editing. Without those, this page shows you the artwork as images.

faqs.question: Does the AI file change when I convert it?
faqs.answer: No. New JPEG files are created and the AI file is read only, so the original is untouched.

guide.title: About AI files
guide.markdown:
### What is an AI file?

A file ending in .ai is Illustrator's native document. Inside are paths, shapes and text drawn as vectors, along with layers, artboards and live effects, and placed raster images can sit among those objects. Logos, illustrations and print layouts are the usual jobs, and brushes, effects and transparency stay editable inside the file.

The format has been through changes: Illustrator 9 reworked it in 2000, and older files used PostScript. Newer files can carry a PDF-compatible copy beside Illustrator's private data, added when you save with the PDF-compatible option. That copy is how other software can draw the artwork without knowing Illustrator's internals.

Illustrator also lets an AI document mix vector objects with pixel images. Two AI files can look alike in a folder and differ inside: one carries the PDF-compatible rendition and the other does not. Third-party software can fail on a file saved without that rendition, because this converter draws the embedded PDF.

### Programs that open AI files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** ImageMagick lists the format as Illustrator CS2 and renders it to a picture instead of editing it.
- **Windows and Mac:** Adobe Illustrator opens native artwork with every object still editable, and it preserves the effects, brushes, layers and transparency stored in the document.
- **Linux:** Inkscape's manual says it imports AI artwork saved by Illustrator 9.0 or later, and some document features may not come across. The same manual notes that an import can open a dialog of options, and that some import formats depend on other programs installed on your computer.

### AI and JPEG compared

- **Extensions**: an Illustrator file ends in .ai; the picture ends in .jpg or .jpeg, two spellings of one format with the image/jpeg media type.
- **Kind of image**: an AI file is mostly vector artwork that can be scaled without losing sharpness. A JPEG is a raster, a fixed grid of pixels, at 8 bits for each color channel.
- **Compression**: JPEG is lossy. In its baseline mode a picture is cut into eight by eight pixel tiles. Each tile is run through a discrete cosine transform before entropy coding with Huffman tables. Progressive files differ by storing several passes, so a viewer can paint a low-detail picture early while downloading continues.
- **Origin**: the format is named for the committee that wrote it. Its core specification is ITU-T T.81, dated 1992, with ISO/IEC 10918-1 as the matching ISO text.
- **Quality**: programs usually expose a 0 to 100 slider, though one number can give different results from one program to the next.
- **Reach**: browsers all show JPEG, and cameras and scanners commonly produce it.
- **Transparency**: Illustrator keeps transparency. JPEG has none and cannot store layers.
- **Editing**: the AI file keeps layers, artboards and live text. A JPEG keeps none of that.

An editable document becomes a flat picture. The page takes the PDF stored inside your AI file, has PDF.js draw each page onto an opaque white background, and writes each one out as a JPEG. The size limits are in the FAQs below. An AI file with no PDF inside cannot be drawn, and the page tells you so.

### Other ways to convert AI to JPEG

- **ImageMagick:** run `magick brand.ai brand-proof.jpeg`. ImageMagick's format list shows AI as readable and says its PDF support requires Ghostscript.

### Problems with AI files

- **An error about a missing PDF**: Illustrator saved the file without its PDF-compatible copy. Reopen it there, turn the PDF-compatible saving option on, and convert the new copy.
- **An old file is refused**: a file from before Illustrator 9 was PostScript-based, so it has no embedded PDF to draw, and this page answers with the no-PDF message. Open it in Illustrator and save it again.
- **Part of the artwork is missing in Inkscape**: Inkscape imports only a subset of the features of some formats, and its manual lists AI files from Illustrator 9.0 onward.
- **Another program draws it wrong**: programs that read only the embedded PDF never see Illustrator's native objects. For editing, use Illustrator.
- **An older Illustrator opens it badly**: Adobe recommends opening artwork in the version that saved it or a newer one.
- **Linked images are missing**: they stay external unless Include Linked Files was selected while saving.

faqs.question: How do I change an AMR to a WAV file?
faqs.answer: Drop your .amr memo on the page above. FFmpeg decodes it inside your browser, and the WAV is ready to save. With several memos you get a WAV per memo.

faqs.question: Why does the WAV weigh so much more than the AMR?
faqs.answer: AMR squeezes a voice into a very small stream. The WAV stores raw 16-bit samples with no compression, and the extra bulk adds no detail.

faqs.question: Will the WAV sound better than the AMR?
faqs.answer: No. Decoding only unpacks the speech into plain samples, and nothing the AMR dropped returns. Narrowband AMR is sampled at just 8 kHz to begin with.

faqs.question: Is the WAV compressed?
faqs.answer: No. The page writes signed 16-bit PCM, so the WAV holds raw samples with no further compression.

faqs.question: My computer won't play .amr. How can I open it?
faqs.answer: FFmpeg decodes AMR from the command line. A WAV from this page opens in Audacity without any extra library.

faqs.question: Where do AMR files come from?
faqs.answer: Mostly from phones: voice recordings and voice messages. ETSI designed the codec for GSM speech before 3GPP took it into third-generation cellular systems.

faqs.question: Is AMR-WB the same codec as AMR?
faqs.answer: They are different codecs. Narrowband works at 8 kHz and AMR-WB at 16 kHz, and each file starts with its own signature, so renaming cannot turn one into the other.

faqs.question: Can I rename a .amr file to .wav?
faqs.answer: No. The file would still hold AMR speech, because changing an extension cannot change the codec inside. Converting writes real WAV data.

faqs.question: Is there a size limit for the AMR file?
faqs.answer: The page sets none, and it has no timeout of its own. FFmpeg runs in your browser, so a longer memo takes longer on a slower device.

faqs.question: What happens if my AMR file is damaged or cut short?
faqs.answer: Most of the time the file still converts. Anything FFmpeg cannot decode is reported and skipped, so the WAV ends up shorter than the original. Fetch a fresh copy from the phone if the end of the recording is missing.

guide.title: About AMR files
guide.markdown:
### What is an AMR file?

Adaptive Multi-Rate, abbreviated AMR, began as an ETSI speech codec for GSM and was later taken up by 3GPP for 3G networks. The codec is tuned for speech and produces tiny files, so phones favor it for voice recordings and voice messages.

A .amr file normally holds the narrowband codec, sampled at 8 kHz and split into 20-millisecond frames with eight speech modes from 4.75 to 12.2 kbps. AMR-WB is its own codec at 16 kHz, with nine wideband modes running from 6.6 to 23.85 kbps. The file starts with a text signature: the characters #!AMR and a line break for narrowband, and #!AMR-WB for wideband. Each stored speech frame then begins with a one-octet header holding a frame type, a quality bit and padding, and the last octet of the speech bits is zero-padded for alignment. A quality bit set to 0 marks a severely damaged frame. A frame that was lost or never transmitted is stored as NO_DATA, and the wideband file can also use SPEECH_LOST. RFC 4867, from April 2007, covers AMR files and their RTP transport, and it registers audio/AMR for narrowband.

You usually meet an AMR file as a recording that came off an older phone, and then find that your computer cannot play it or your editor will not import it. Audacity imports WAV, so a WAV copy gets around that.

Archivists at the Library of Congress list WAVE among recommended formats for audio collections, which suits a recording you mean to keep.

### Programs that open AMR files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** FFmpeg is a command-line tool with decoders for AMR narrowband and AMR wideband.

### AMR and WAV compared

- **Extensions and media types**: .amr and audio/AMR for narrowband AMR; .wav and audio/wav or audio/x-wav for WAV.
- **Kind of format**: AMR names a speech codec, whereas WAV is a RIFF wrapper that can hold several encodings, usually linear PCM but sometimes compressed ones.
- **Compression**: AMR is lossy and tuned for speech. PCM in WAV is uncompressed.
- **Frames**: an AMR file is a run of 20-millisecond speech frames, each with its own small header. A WAV stores a continuous stream of samples, so the frame structure disappears in the conversion.
- **Bandwidth**: AMR suits a voice and little else. WAV can hold much wider audio, but a WAV made from AMR still carries only what the AMR kept.
- **Limits and metadata**: a WAV has a 4 GB size limit, and very large recordings may need RF64 rather than the original RIFF size fields. Broadcast WAVE adds production and preservation metadata, and since extension chunks and the standard INFO chunks hold different information, programs treat them differently.

What changes in this conversion is the storage, not the sound. The page runs FFmpeg in a worker and writes 16-bit PCM. The result is a plain waveform. Audacity opens nearly every WAV, all PCM variants included, with no extra library, but a WAV with a recorder's proprietary compression is a case where Audacity recommends its FFmpeg library. It does not reverse the speech compression, and raising the sampling rate in another program afterward cannot put missing frequencies back.

### Other ways to convert AMR to WAV

- **FFmpeg:** run `ffmpeg -i memo.amr memo-edit.wav`. FFmpeg's codec documentation lists decoders for AMR narrowband and wideband, and says the AMR-NB one is built into FFmpeg itself.

### Problems with AMR files

- **The sound is thin or tinny**: that is the codec. A narrowband recording cannot supply the wider frequency range of an AMR-WB source, because the two use different sampling rates.
- **You are not sure what it is**: check the first bytes. A narrowband file begins with #!AMR and a line break, and a wideband file with #!AMR-WB.
- **Renaming did not work**: AMR and AMR-WB signatures differ, and changing an extension cannot change the encoded speech.
- **The WAV is far larger than the AMR**: AMR packs speech into a few kilobits a second, while a WAV holds every sample as uncompressed PCM, so the file grows even though no detail is added.
- **The recording is cut off**: a partial transfer from the phone gives a partial recording. This page usually still turns the part that arrived into a shorter WAV, but copy the file across again for the whole memo.

infoArticle.title: About audio and video transcription
infoArticle.markdown:
Audio to Text transcribes speech from audio or video files. Uploaded files are processed in your browser. If you paste a direct link to an audio or video file, the server fetches the file and streams it to your browser for transcription. YouTube, TikTok, SoundCloud, and other webpage links are not supported right now. The speech model downloads on first use and runs locally.

This tool is best for interviews, meetings, lectures, and voice notes. Larger files take longer to process and may use more memory.

**Why use this tool**

- Handles uploads or direct links to audio and video files.
- Creates a plain text transcript you can edit or share.
- Works with common audio and video formats.

faqs.question: Do my files get uploaded?
faqs.answer: Uploads are processed locally in your browser. If you paste a direct link to an audio or video file, the server fetches the file and streams it to your browser. The model files are downloaded when needed.

faqs.question: Which file types are supported?
faqs.answer: Common audio and video formats like MP3, WAV, M4A, AAC, FLAC, OGG, OPUS, MP4, MOV, MKV, WEBM, AVI, and M4V.

faqs.question: Can I use YouTube or SoundCloud links?
faqs.answer: Not right now. YouTube, SoundCloud, TikTok, and other webpage links are not supported. Upload the audio or video file, or paste a direct link to one.

faqs.question: Why is the first run slower?
faqs.answer: The speech model downloads the first time you run the tool. After that it is cached for faster use.

faqs.question: How do I turn an AV1 video into an MP4?
faqs.answer: Add the .av1 file in the box above. Your browser decodes the AV1, the page encodes H.264 into an MP4, and you save the result. A batch is processed one file at a time.

faqs.question: Does the MP4 keep AV1 video?
faqs.answer: No. The MP4 holds H.264 video, which more players, phones and editors decode than AV1. To keep AV1 inside an MP4 without re-encoding, use one of the desktop methods listed in the guide.

faqs.question: Why does the MP4 have no sound?
faqs.answer: A .av1 file is a bare video stream, so no audio track exists to carry over, and the page labels it "Video only". If the sound lives in another file, combine the two in a video editor.

faqs.question: Why does it say my browser can't decode AV1?
faqs.answer: Decoding is done by the AV1 decoder built into your browser, and some devices lack one. You then see "Your browser can't decode AV1 on this device" and a suggestion to try a current Chrome or Edge on another computer.

faqs.question: Does the MP4 keep the AV1's resolution and frame rate?
faqs.answer: Up to a ceiling, yes. Bigger pictures shrink to fit under the ceiling, while smaller ones stay as they are. A clip with a higher frame rate than the ceiling has frames removed, and its running time stays the same. Rounding to even sizes can trim one pixel from an odd width or height.

faqs.question: Does the MP4 look as good as the AV1?
faqs.answer: Not identically. The AV1 is decoded and the pictures go through a new H.264 encode, so the MP4 is a fresh encode in a different lossy codec, not a copy.

faqs.question: What is a .av1 file?
faqs.answer: It is the AV1 codec's raw stream saved straight to disk. Online video usually wraps AV1 in MP4 or WebM instead, and the .av1 ending is optional, so a suffix tells you nothing about the framing.

faqs.question: Can I open an AV1 file without converting it?
faqs.answer: FFmpeg supports AV1 through external libraries, such as libaom and libdav1d. Converting it to an MP4 here gives you an ordinary file for any player.

faqs.question: Is there a way to convert AV1 to MP4 without re-encoding?
faqs.answer: Yes, on a desktop. MP4Box and an FFmpeg stream copy both put the AV1 into an MP4 as it is, and the result still needs a player with an AV1 decoder.

faqs.question: What is the download called?
faqs.answer: The MP4 is saved under your file's name with an .mp4 ending: scene.av1 becomes scene.mp4.

guide.title: About AV1 files
guide.markdown:
### What is an AV1 file?

AV1 stands for AOMedia Video 1. It is a video codec, not a complete movie format. The Alliance for Open Media developed its bitstream and decoding specification, and the Library of Congress describes it as an open, royalty-free video coding format. The public release of the specification was announced on March 28, 2018.

An AV1 bitstream is organized into units called OBUs. Its registered media type is video/av1, and it supports full-resolution chroma setups such as 4:4:4. A .av1 file on this page's input side is that bare stream: video only, with no audio track and nothing wrapped around it. Most of the AV1 you meet sits inside an MP4 or WebM file.

AV1 has no required file extension, so the ending alone cannot tell you the framing. A raw stream of OBUs and an AV1 image container are different inputs, and FFmpeg documents them as separate formats. AV1 encoding can take longer than older codecs because its compression process is complex. You get a .av1 file from an encoder such as aomenc, or from a tool that writes out a video stream on its own.

### Programs that open AV1 files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** FFmpeg supports AV1 through external libraries, among them libaom, libdav1d, librav1e and libsvtav1.

### AV1 and MP4 compared

- **What each is**: AV1 is a codec. MP4, defined in ISO/IEC 14496-14, is a container that can hold H.264, H.265 or AV1 video along with audio.
- **Sound**: a .av1 stream has none, so an MP4 made from it has none either.
- **Reach**: H.264 is the video most phones, editors and upload forms handle. AV1 depends on a decoder, which some devices lack.
- **Playback**: a container that FFmpeg or a player accepts does not guarantee a decoder for the video inside it.
- **Extensions**: .av1 has no required extension; .mp4 is the container's.
- **Safety of the file**: a standard MP4 holds its index data in one place, so an interrupted write can leave a file that no player opens.

Both the codec and the wrapper change. Your browser decodes the AV1 with its built-in decoder, and the page writes H.264 into the MP4. The picture is capped at 1920 pixels along its longer edge and 30 frames per second. Frames are removed from a faster clip, which keeps the running time, and since the encoder needs even sizes, a side with an odd pixel count gets one pixel trimmed. All of this runs in your browser, so the video never leaves your device, and each file in a batch gets its own MP4.

That also explains the wait: the page decodes, re-encodes and scales entirely on your device, and several files run one after another. The MP4 has no sound.

### Other ways to convert AV1 to MP4

- **GPAC MP4Box:** run `MP4Box -add scene.av1 scene-av1.mp4`. This keeps AV1 inside the MP4. The GPAC article says to add `:fps=1000` if the stream carries no timing, and `:fmt=obu` if the extension is not recognized. It accepts OBU, IVF and Annex B framing, and it does not accept WebM.
- **FFmpeg, stream copy:** run `ffmpeg -i clip.av1 -c:v copy -an clip-copy.mp4`. Copying skips decoding and encoding, so the AV1 is untouched, and the MP4 still needs an AV1 decoder to play.
- **FFmpeg, H.264:** run `ffmpeg -i scene.av1 -c:v libx264 -an scene-h264.mp4`. The `-an` option leaves out any audio, and libx264 writes the H.264.

### Problems with AV1 files

- **"Your browser can't decode AV1"**: your device has no AV1 decoder for the browser to use. Try a recent Chrome or Edge on a different computer, or use FFmpeg.
- **The file will not play**: the suffix does not tell you the framing. A raw OBU stream and an IVF file differ, so name the framing yourself when you import it.
- **The speed looks wrong in another tool**: a raw stream may carry little timing information, which a container-based player expects. When you import it yourself, pass the frame rate on purpose instead of guessing it from the duration.
- **An audio editor shows nothing**: an MP4 without audio cannot provide an audio track to an editor, and a .av1 stream never had one.
- **Encoding takes a while**: AV1's compression process is complex, so a longer clip takes longer.

seo.title: Convert AVI to MKV Online (Free)
seo.description: Convert AVI video to MKV in your browser. The video is re-encoded as H.264 with AAC sound, not copied, so the MKV is a compressed copy. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.question: How do I convert AVI to MKV?
faqs.answer: Select your AVI, let the converter run and save the MKV it returns. A batch is processed in order, and each MKV downloads on its own.

faqs.question: Is this a lossless AVI to MKV remux?
faqs.answer: No. The video is decoded and encoded again, with 96 kbps AAC sound added. For a container swap without re-encoding, run FFmpeg yourself with -c copy.

faqs.question: Could the MKV look worse than my AVI?
faqs.answer: It can, because the video is compressed a second time at a fixed, speed-first setting that you cannot adjust.

faqs.question: Will the MKV be smaller than the AVI?
faqs.answer: It can be, but nothing guarantees it. The page re-encodes at fixed settings with no size target, so the result depends on the codec inside the AVI. In one test run a small AVI came out smaller.

faqs.question: Which audio tracks end up in the MKV?
faqs.answer: No -map option is given, so FFmpeg's defaults decide which streams are written. With an unusual AVI layout, play the MKV first and only then delete the original.

faqs.question: Why would I move from AVI to MKV?
faqs.answer: Matroska is designed for many streams (video, audio, subtitles) plus chapters and tags in one file, and it does not tie you to one codec. AVI is an older RIFF container.

faqs.question: Will resolution and frame rate stay as they were?
faqs.answer: Within limits. A frame whose longer side passes 1920 pixels is scaled down, the rate never exceeds 30 fps, and a pixel is trimmed from any odd side. Smaller footage keeps its size.

faqs.question: What plays an MKV file?
faqs.answer: VLC media player and mpv play MKV on desktop, ffplay can too, and VLC's Android and iOS apps play it on phones. Whether a given file plays still depends on the codecs inside it.

faqs.question: Can I rename an AVI to .mkv instead?
faqs.answer: No. A rename only changes the label. AVI is a RIFF file and Matroska is built on EBML, so the contents do not match the name. Converting writes a real Matroska file.

faqs.question: Is my AVI uploaded anywhere?
faqs.answer: No. The video never travels anywhere: FFmpeg, built for WebAssembly, runs in your browser to make the MKV. Your AVI file is not modified, and the MKV arrives as a separate download.

guide.title: About AVI files
guide.markdown:
### What is an AVI file?

Windows 3.1 got AVI, short for Audio Video Interleave, from Microsoft, with a first specification from 1992. Pictures and sound that run on a timeline are stored in a RIFF file. One chunk holds the header (dimensions, frame rate and similar), another holds the media, and FOURCC codes name each stream and codec.

Uncompressed, lossless or lossy video can all live in an AVI, so the extension alone cannot tell you its quality or size. The usual ending is .avi, and one common media-type label is video/x-msvideo.

You find AVI in video production archives and in older desktop workflows such as camera and capture output. It is a legacy container, and people often replace it with something newer.

### Programs that open AVI files

QuickTime Player, VLC and Windows Media Player all play AVI. Sorted by platform, the fact sheet for AVI names these programs:

**Windows, Mac and Linux**

- ffplay: FFmpeg contains the AVI demuxer.
- mpv: desktop playback where audio and subtitle streams are selectable.

**Windows and Mac**

- Adobe Premiere: takes in the container so long as the decoder it needs is there.

**Mobile**

- VLC for Android and VLC for iOS: the Android app is free, and what it decodes follows from the contents of the container; the iOS app is a mobile player that handles most movie formats and reaches both local and network media.

### AVI and MKV compared

- **Names and types**: .avi is commonly labeled video/x-msvideo, and IANA registers video/matroska for Matroska video.
- **Structure**: AVI is built from RIFF chunks. Matroska rests on EBML, a binary structure that derives from XML.
- **Tracks**: Matroska can carry several video, audio and subtitle streams, and chapters and descriptive tags are part of its design. AVI has limited support for modern features.
- **Codecs**: no codec or quality level is built into either container. An AVI may hold uncompressed, lossless or lossy video, and Matroska leaves the compression method open.
- **Origins**: Microsoft introduced AVI in 1992. Matroska developed from the earlier MCF project.

This page does not just rewrap the AVI. It decodes the video and writes it again through x264 at CRF 32 with its ultrafast preset, writes the sound as 96 kbps AAC, scales anything past 1920 pixels along the longer edge, and holds the rate to 30 fps. The MKV is a compressed copy, not an archival match of the AVI, and you cannot change the quality.

No stream mapping is passed, so FFmpeg's own defaults pick the streams, and its defaults also copy global tags where the output can hold them. For a plain one-video, one-audio AVI that is what you expect. Your original stays untouched, and the download is named after the AVI with the .mkv ending. Pick several files and they convert in turn, one MKV each. This page does not cap the size.

### Other ways to convert AVI to MKV

- **FFmpeg, remux (Windows, Mac, Linux):** run `ffmpeg -i capture-master.avi -c copy capture-master.mkv`. Streams are copied without re-encoding, and FFmpeg chooses them automatically.
- **HandBrakeCLI:** run `HandBrakeCLI --input avi-review.avi --output avi-review.mkv --format av_mkv --encoder x264 --aencoder av_aac --quality 22`. This re-encodes, so it is a derivative copy.
- **Prism (Windows):** add the AVI, set Output Format to MKV, review Encoder Options, set Save to Folder and click Convert. Its available codecs depend on the installation.

### Problems with AVI files

- **The player opens it but an editor rejects it**: an editor may identify AVI yet have no decoder for what is actually inside.
- **A huge capture won't open**: the original AVI design limits size in ways the later OpenDML extension does not, so big captures need software that copes.
- **Stretched or combed picture**: implementations of AVI do not treat aspect ratio and scan type in a consistent way. Check the MKV in a player.
- **Wrong or missing extra track**: this page does not map tracks, and FFmpeg's defaults decide. Run FFmpeg yourself if you need a specific stream layout.
- **A damaged or cut-short AVI**: it often converts anyway, yielding a shorter MKV. Compare its running time with the source.
- **A smaller picture than the source**: this page scales footage whose longer side passes 1920 pixels. The FFmpeg remux keeps the original size.
- **A soft or blocky result**: the page re-encodes at CRF 32 with the ultrafast preset, so the MKV can look worse than the AVI.

faqs.question: Can you convert AVI to MP4 without re-encoding?

guide.title: Understanding AVI to MPG
guide.markdown:
### What is an AVI file?

Microsoft introduced AVI, a RIFF container, alongside Windows 3.1, and the first specification dates from 1992. FOURCC codes name each stream's codec, and the header stores properties such as dimensions and frame rate. The video inside may be raw, lossless or lossy, which means .avi alone says nothing about quality. Production archives and older desktop workflows still hold many of these files.

### Programs that open AVI files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** FFplay and mpv play AVI.
- **Windows and Mac:** Adobe Premiere imports it when a matching decoder exists.
- **Mobile:** AVI files open in VLC's Android and iOS apps.

### AVI and MPG compared

- **MPG**: a suffix for MPEG video. MPEG-2 began as a standard for compressing television and later became the video format on DVDs.
- **Video**: MPEG-2, from the FFmpeg `mpeg2video` encoder, so the picture is encoded again.
- **Audio**: MP2 at 96 kbps, also encoded again from the AVI's sound.
- **Picture size**: the longer side stops at 1920 px, and both dimensions are made even.
- **Motion**: no more than 30 fps, and interlaced frames pass through a deinterlacer.
- **Disc**: the result is a media file with no menus or DVD folders.
- **Streams and tags**: with no stream mapping given, FFmpeg's defaults decide which streams go in, and global tags are copied where the MPG can hold them.
- **Length**: frames above 30 fps are dropped, but the clip keeps its length.
- **Privacy**: the conversion happens on your device, so the AVI never leaves it.

### Other ways to convert AVI to MPG

- **FFmpeg:** run `ffmpeg -i tape-capture.avi -c:a mp2 -q:v 4 -c:v mpeg2video recording.mpg`. FFmpeg takes the encoders from `-c:v` and `-c:a`, a fixed quality scale from `-q`, and the output format from the .mpg extension.

### Problems with AVI files

- **A tool recognizes the AVI yet cannot decode it**: it understands the container but lacks the decoder for the contents.
- **A large capture fails**: the original AVI layout limits file size and OpenDML extended it, so big captures need software that supports the extension.
- **Aspect ratio or scan type is wrong**: AVI implementations handle those flags inconsistently. Check the MPG before deleting the AVI.

guide.title: AVI to WAV: format guide
guide.markdown:
### What is an AVI file?

Microsoft introduced AVI alongside Windows 3.1, and the first specification is from 1992. It is a RIFF file that carries timed pictures and sound. The header records properties such as dimensions and frame rate, and another chunk stores the media. Each stream's codec is named by a FOURCC code.

AVI carries video that may be uncompressed, lossless or lossy; the file extension says little about its quality. You meet AVI in video production archives and older desktop video workflows. People convert AVI to WAV to get the soundtrack into an audio editor, away from the picture.

### Programs that open AVI files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** ffplay plays AVI, and mpv plays it too, with selectable audio streams.
- **Windows and Mac:** Adobe Premiere imports AVI once a decoder for its contents is available.
- **Mobile:** The mobile players VLC for Android and VLC for iOS handle AVI, though decoding depends on what the container holds.

### AVI and WAV compared

An AVI interleaves video and audio. A WAV is an audio wrapper, usually holding uncompressed PCM, so it is lossless but large. A WAV file also tops out at 4 GB. This page asks FFmpeg for 16-bit PCM and drops the video, so a soundtrack stored at a higher bit depth is written at 16 bits. The WAV keeps what the AVI's audio codec decoded, and nothing more.

### Other ways to convert AVI to WAV

- **FFmpeg (command line):** enter `ffmpeg -i input.avi -vn output.wav`. `-vn` drops the video, and `-map` lets you pick one audio stream.

### Problems with AVI files

- **An editor opens the AVI but cannot decode it**: an editor can recognize AVI and still lack the decoder for its particular contents. Install the matching decoder or play it in VLC.
- **A large capture will not open**: size limits differ between original AVI and the later OpenDML extension, so a large capture may need compatible software.
- **The picture shape looks wrong**: programs read the aspect ratio and scan type stored in an AVI inconsistently.
- **No sound here**: the AVI has no audio track, and the converter reports an FFmpeg error. A picture that plays does not prove there is sound.

guide.title: About AVI files
guide.markdown:
### What is an AVI file?

With Windows 3.1, Microsoft brought out Audio Video Interleave; the first specification followed in 1992. A RIFF file stores the timed pictures and sound, and a header in it notes things like size and frame rate. Another chunk contains the media, and FOURCC identifiers label every stream and codec.

Because the container leaves the codec open, the video inside can be uncompressed, lossless or lossy, and the .avi ending reveals nothing about quality. A commonly used media-type label is video/x-msvideo.

AVI turns up in archived footage and in old Windows video, whether camera or capture output. It is a legacy format with limited support for modern features.

### Programs that open AVI files

AVI opens in Windows Media Player, QuickTime Player and VLC. By platform, the format's fact sheet adds:

**Windows, Mac and Linux**

- ffplay: the AVI demuxer ships with FFmpeg.
- mpv: desktop player where you select audio and subtitle streams.

**Windows and Mac**

- Adobe Premiere: opens the container provided the required decoder is present.

**Mobile**

- VLC for Android and VLC for iOS: on Android it is free, and whether a file decodes hinges on the media inside the container; on iOS it is a phone and tablet player for most movie formats, covering local files and network media.

### AVI and WebM compared

- **Labels**: .avi is commonly tagged video/x-msvideo. WebM video uses video/webm, and an audio-only WebM uses audio/webm.
- **Structure**: AVI is RIFF chunks. WebM is based on Matroska, which is built on EBML.
- **Codecs**: AVI may hold uncompressed, lossless or lossy video. For WebM the picture is VP8 or VP9 (AV1 video is allowed too), with Vorbis or Opus as the sound.
- **Licensing**: the WebM Project supplies its format technology under royalty-free terms.
- **Browser reach**: major browsers support WebM, and Chrome, Firefox and Edge open it.
- **Age**: Microsoft introduced AVI in 1992, and WebM is an open format promoted for web delivery.

This page decodes the AVI and writes a new WebM. The video is VP8 from libvpx at CRF 40 in its realtime mode with the fastest CPU setting, written as 8-bit yuv420p. The sound is Vorbis at 64 kbps. A picture past 1920 pixels along its longer edge is scaled down, and a quicker source is thinned to 30 frames per second without changing how long it lasts. The settings favor speed over detail, so keep the AVI if quality may matter later.

FFmpeg's defaults decide which streams go in, since nothing is mapped by hand. Your AVI is never changed, and the download is named after it with the .webm ending. The page applies no size limit, so a long file simply keeps a slower device busy for longer. Pick several files and they convert in turn.

### Other ways to convert AVI to WebM

- **FFmpeg on a desktop:** run `ffmpeg -i web-source.avi -c:v libvpx-vp9 -b:v 1024k -crf 32 -c:a libopus web-delivery.webm` for VP9 and Opus in constrained-quality mode, which Google's VP9 guide recommends for on-demand video. The result is lossy.
- **HandBrake (Windows, Mac, Linux):** choose the AVI under Open Source, then set the container to WebM. HandBrake lists VP8, VP9 and AV1 video encoders for WebM, with Vorbis or Opus audio.
- **Prism (Windows):** add the file, choose WebM as the output, set the encoder and folder, then click Convert. NCH lists AVI as an input and WebM as an output.

### Problems with AVI files

- **An editor shows black frames or silence**: an editor can know AVI and still have no decoder for the specific contents.
- **Two AVI files look nothing alike**: the file name does not reveal quality, since the contents may be uncompressed, lossless or lossy.
- **The WebM looks soft in motion**: the page trades detail for speed. The FFmpeg command above uses VP9 and a quality target instead.
- **The WebM plays in one browser and not another**: what plays is set by the real video and audio codecs, and the .webm suffix alone settles nothing.
- **Seeking feels slow**: without a cue index, seeking can be less efficient, since the player has less direct information about where things are.
- **An old Safari will not play it**: macOS Safari gained WebM playback in version 14.1 for VP8 or VP9 video with Vorbis sound, so do not assume older releases play it.
- **Wrong picture shape**: AVI implementations differ in how they treat aspect ratio and scan type. Check the result in a player.
- **A very large AVI fails to open**: the first AVI design has size restrictions that the later OpenDML extension does not, so large captures need compatible software.
- **A damaged or cut-short AVI**: it commonly converts all the same, giving a shorter WebM. Compare its running time with the source.

guide.title: About AVI files
guide.markdown:
### What is an AVI file?

AVI, short for Audio Video Interleave, is a RIFF container that Microsoft introduced with Windows 3.1 in 1992. Streams inside it are labeled with FOURCC codes, so the .avi extension reveals neither the codec nor the picture quality. Size limits in the first specification are not the ones OpenDML later allowed, which is why a long capture needs software that supports it.

Legacy Windows clips, footage straight from cameras and capture devices, and archives are where AVI shows up. WMV is the target when an older Windows workflow expects Windows Media Video.

### Programs that open AVI files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** FFplay, FFmpeg's own player, plays AVI, and mpv offers desktop playback.
- **Windows and Mac:** Adobe Premiere on both can import AVI, provided it has a decoder for what the file holds.
- **Mobile:** VLC for Android is a free player, though what it can show hinges on the streams within the file, and VLC for iOS handles most movie formats along with local and network media.

### AVI and WMV compared

- **Extensions and media types**: .avi with video/x-msvideo; .wmv with video/x-ms-wmv, a label the Library of Congress records as commonly used, not an IANA registration.
- **Container**: AVI is a RIFF container able to wrap many different codecs. A .wmv file uses Microsoft's ASF container with Windows Media coded content.
- **Typical use**: AVI is found in legacy Windows clips and archived footage. WMV carried older Windows video, screencasts and Windows Media broadcasts.

Here FFmpeg decodes the AVI and writes a new WMV. It deinterlaces the picture, scales the longer side to at most 1920 px with even dimensions, and caps the frame rate at 30 fps. The audio is re-encoded as well, so nothing is copied across untouched. The command names no codec, so FFmpeg's defaults decide, and a detailed picture can come out soft.

### Other ways to convert AVI to WMV

- **FFmpeg:** run `ffmpeg -i capture.avi -c:v wmv2 -c:a wmav2 archive.wmv` to pick FFmpeg's Windows Media Video and Windows Media Audio encoders yourself. This re-encodes both streams.

### Problems with AVI files

A black picture with working sound means the player lacks the video codec; the file is not empty. Opening it in a second player with its own decoders tells you which case you have.

Aspect ratio and scan type are recorded inconsistently across AVI implementations. A picture that looks stretched or combed in one player may look right in another, so judge the WMV in the same player you used for the AVI.

faqs.question: Why do websites use AVIF?
faqs.answer: The format is royalty-free and its files are small for the detail they keep, so sites send it to browsers that support it and fall back to JPG or PNG for the rest.

guide.title: About AVIF files
guide.markdown:
### What is an AVIF file?

AVIF, the AV1 Image File Format, stores pictures compressed with the AV1 video codec inside a HEIF container, the same container family iPhone photos use. It comes from the Alliance for Open Media, a group founded in 2015 to build royalty-free media formats, which published AV1 in 2018. Version 1.0.0 of the AVIF specification is dated 19 February 2019.

AVIF can be lossy or lossless, keep transparency, hold image sequences and store up to 12 bits per channel for HDR and wide color gamut. The cost is speed: AVIF images are slow to decode, encoding one can take several seconds, and they don't draw progressively while loading.

An AVIF image sequence can stand in for an animated GIF at a fraction of the size. You mostly find AVIF on the web, where sites send it to browsers that can show it. Save such a picture and you get an .avif file that many editors, upload forms and older devices can't use.

### Programs that open AVIF files

**Windows**

- Photos: shows AVIF once the AV1 Video Extension and the HEIF Image Extension are installed from the Microsoft Store.
- GIMP: imports and exports AVIF from version 2.10.22, released in October 2020.

**Mac**

- GIMP: the same AVIF support as on Windows.
- ImageMagick: converts AVIF from Terminal.

**Linux**

- GIMP: the main desktop editor for AVIF.
- avifdec: the command-line decoder that ships with libavif.

**Web**

- Chrome 85+, Firefox 93+, Safari 16.1+ and Edge 121+ display AVIF. This page relies on that support, since your browser does the decoding.

**Mobile**

- Android: decodes AVIF from Android 12.
- Phone browsers: current Chrome on Android and Safari on iPhone show AVIF pages.

### AVIF and JPG compared

- **Extensions and media types**: .avif with image/avif; .jpg or .jpeg with image/jpeg.
- **Compression**: AVIF uses AV1's intra-frame coding, lossy or lossless. JPEG cuts the picture into 8x8 blocks, and its baseline mode is always lossy.
- **Color depth**: AVIF goes up to 12 bits per channel, with HDR and wide gamut. JPEG stores 8 bits per channel.
- **Transparency**: AVIF has an alpha channel. JPG has none.
- **Sequences**: AVIF can hold an animation. A JPG holds one frame.
- **Size**: in AVIF's Baseline profile one AV1 image is at most 8,192 x 4,352 pixels, and a larger picture is stored as a grid of such tiles. A JPEG can measure up to 65,535 pixels a side.
- **Loading**: a progressive JPEG shows a coarse version first and sharpens. AVIF appears only once decoded.
- **Licensing**: AVIF is royalty-free, and JPEG's US patents expired in 2006.
- **Metadata**: both carry Exif, XMP and an ICC profile; this converter keeps none of them.

The JPG gives up AVIF's small file and extra color precision in return for reach: almost every program, device and upload form takes it. This page decodes the AVIF with your browser and writes the JPG at quality 0.85.

### Other ways to convert AVIF to JPG

- **GIMP (Windows, Mac, Linux)**: open the AVIF in version 2.10.22 or later, choose File > Export As, name the file with .jpg and click Export.
- **ImageMagick (command line)**: run `magick input.avif output.jpg`.
- **avifdec from libavif (command line)**: run `avifdec input.avif output.jpg`. The `-q` option sets the JPEG quality, 90 by default. Only the first frame of a sequence is decoded unless `--index` names another frame, or all of them.

### Problems with AVIF files

- **"This browser can't open … files"**: your browser has no AVIF decoder. Update it, or switch to Chrome 85+, Firefox 93+, Safari 16.1+ or Edge 121+.
- **Windows Photos shows nothing**: add the AV1 Video Extension and the HEIF Image Extension.
- **A big image takes a while**: AVIF decodes slowly by design, so give a large file a moment.
- **See-through areas are lost**: JPG has no alpha channel. The [AVIF to PNG converter](/avif-to-png/) keeps transparency.
- **An animation gives one picture**: a JPG holds a single frame, so only the first is kept.
- **Changed the ending by hand**: an AVIF renamed to .jpg still holds AV1 data, and JPEG readers reject it.
- **An upload form says the file type isn't allowed**: many forms list only JPG, PNG and GIF. Upload the JPG made here instead.

guide.title: About AVIF files
guide.markdown:
### What is an AVIF file?

Most AVIF files people want to convert were saved from a web page. Image services and content delivery networks send AVIF to browsers that support it because the files are small, so a picture that looked ordinary on a site lands on disk as .avif and then won't go into a slide deck, an older editor or an upload form.

Underneath, AVIF, the AV1 Image File Format, is HEIF: a structure of boxes that holds image items and their properties. Each picture is compressed with AV1, the royalty-free video codec the Alliance for Open Media released in 2018, and version 1.0.0 of the AVIF specification followed on 19 February 2019.

Transparency gets an item of its own. The alpha plane is coded as a separate auxiliary image tied to the main picture, which is how an AVIF logo or cut-out keeps soft, partly see-through edges. A file can also hold an image sequence, Exif, XMP and an ICC profile, at up to 12 bits per channel. Decoding all of this is slow, and an AVIF appears only once it is fully decoded instead of sharpening as it loads.

### Programs that open AVIF files

**Windows**

- Edge and Chrome: open an .avif dragged into a tab, with no add-ons.
- Photos: needs two Microsoft Store add-ons, the HEIF Image Extension and the AV1 Video Extension, before it shows AVIF.
- GIMP: reads and writes AVIF from release 2.10.22.

**Mac**

- Safari, Chrome and Firefox: view AVIF files.
- ImageMagick: turns an AVIF into a PNG with one Terminal command.

**Linux**

- GIMP and ImageMagick: open and convert AVIF.
- avifdec: libavif's own decoder, which can write a 16-bit PNG.

**Web**

- Current versions of every major browser: Chrome from 85, Firefox from 93, Safari from 16.1 and Edge from 121.

**Mobile**

- Android: AVIF decoding is built in from Android 12.
- iPhone and iPad: Safari shows AVIF on current iOS versions.

### AVIF and PNG compared

- **Extensions and media types**: .avif with image/avif; .png with image/png.
- **Compression**: AVIF codes each picture with AV1's still-image tools, with or without loss. PNG filters every row of pixels and packs it with DEFLATE, never losing anything.
- **Transparency**: both have a full alpha channel. AVIF keeps it as an auxiliary image beside the picture; PNG stores it with every pixel. This converter keeps it.
- **Bit depth**: AVIF reaches 12 bits per channel and PNG up to 16, but the PNG made here has 8 bits per channel, so HDR and extra depth don't survive.
- **File size**: for a photo, a PNG is often several times the size of the AVIF. For flat graphics the gap is smaller.
- **Animation**: an AVIF can be an image sequence; this page converts its first frame only.
- **Metadata**: AVIF can carry Exif, XMP and an ICC profile. None of them is copied into the PNG.
- **Support**: nearly every program opens PNG. AVIF needs a fairly recent browser, viewer or editor.

Choose PNG when you need transparency, crisp edges or a file you will edit and save again. For photos you only want to share, the [AVIF to JPG converter](/avif-to-jpg/) gives a much smaller file, and [AVIF to WebP](/avif-to-webp/) keeps transparency at a smaller size than PNG.

### Other ways to convert AVIF to PNG

- **GIMP (Windows, Mac, Linux)**: GIMP 2.10.22 or newer opens the AVIF; then choose File > Export As, end the name with .png and click Export.
- **ImageMagick (command line)**: `magick input.avif output.png` writes the PNG in one step.
- **avifdec (command line)**: run `avifdec input.avif output.png`, adding `-d 8` or `-d 16` to choose 8 or 16 bits per channel. A 16-bit PNG keeps more of an HDR picture's depth than this page does. For an image sequence it decodes frame one unless `--index` asks for a different frame or for every frame.

### Problems with AVIF files

- **Windows shows a blank thumbnail or won't open the file**: add Microsoft's HEIF Image Extension and AV1 Video Extension from the Microsoft Store, or open the AVIF in a browser.
- **"This browser can't open AVIF files"**: there is no AVIF decoder in your browser. Updating usually fixes it, and any current Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari works.
- **The PNG is far bigger than expected**: a photo stored losslessly is heavy. Convert photos to JPG or WebP instead.
- **An animation became a still picture**: only the first frame is converted. Keep the AVIF, or use a tool that writes animated output.
- **Colors look duller than in the browser**: the PNG has 8 bits per channel and no color profile, so HDR and wide-color highlights are lost.
- **"Image decode failed."**: the file is damaged or isn't really an AVIF. Save it again from its source.

guide.title: Understanding BIN to JPG
guide.markdown:
### What is a BIN file?

The .bin extension is a catch-all for files holding raw binary data. The contents can be an image, a disc image, firmware or an email attachment, so the real type depends on the file. It has no fixed structure.

For this page, the useful cases are pictures saved under a .bin name. Outlook writes attachments as ATT00001.bin, a browser download can be saved as .bin, and a Mac file in MacBinary uses the same extension.

### Programs that open BIN files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** UltraEdit provides a hex view for .bin files, though that does not decode every BIN, and GNU Emacs Hexl inspects and edits the bytes through hexl-find-file.
- **Web:** HexEd.it offers browser-based byte inspection and editing, but it is not a universal BIN interpreter.

### BIN and JPG compared

- **Detection**: the page looks at the first bytes of the file, up to 4096, and picks the engine for the picture it finds. A MacBinary file is read past its 128-byte header.
- **Refusal**: a file with no picture signature is refused from its first bytes alone, so a disc image of several gigabytes is never read whole.
- **Transparency**: a JPG cannot store alpha, so see-through pixels cannot be kept.
- **Damaged pictures**: a file that starts like a picture but cannot be decoded fails with a message saying so.
- **Original**: your BIN is not changed. You download a new JPG.

### Other ways to convert BIN to JPG

- **Pillow:** in Python, `Image.open("photo.bin")` opens and identifies the file, `.convert("RGB")` changes the mode, and `.save("photo.jpg")` picks the JPEG format from the file name.
- **ImageMagick:** run `magick photo.bin recovered.jpg`. It works only on a file ImageMagick can read as a picture.

### Problems with BIN files

- **A disc image or firmware file is refused**: those hold no picture, so no converter can turn them into a JPG.
- **Raw samples have no picture layout**: a BIN of raw numbers carries no width, height or pixel arrangement, so nothing can draw it as an image.
- **A hex editor can change the file**: look inside a BIN on a copy, because saving edited bytes alters it.
- **You do not know what the file is**: check the source of the attachment, since a .bin name says nothing about the content.

### What is a BMP file?

BMP is a raster image family that Microsoft controls, first seen on Windows and OS/2. Version 5 of the format shipped with Windows 98 in 1998 and added an ICC profile plus an alpha channel. Pixels are commonly stored uncompressed, though lossless compression exists. It is registered as image/bmp.

Windows screen captures and system graphics are where BMP is commonly encountered.

### Programs that open BMP files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** ImageMagick reads BMP images. XnView MP also lists BMP among its supported formats; company use requires a license.
- **Web:** Mozilla Firefox displays BMP pictures in browser content, and Google Chrome is listed as supporting BMP in Mozilla's compatibility data.

### BMP and ICO compared

- **Names and media types**: .bmp with image/bmp; .ico with image/vnd.microsoft.icon.
- **What each holds**: a BMP is one picture. An ICO file can bundle several images and stores its numbers little-endian.
- **Where ICO is used**: Microsoft's graphical interface icons and website favicons. Windows Vista icon guidance adds a larger image for high-DPI displays.

The ICO written here has one image only, and ImageMagick writes it from the decoded pixels. When the BMP is taller or wider than 256 px, it is fitted inside a square of that size with its proportions kept; a smaller one is left at its own size and not enlarged. A full-size image is stored as PNG data inside the ICO. The color profile and other metadata are dropped.

### Other ways to convert BMP to ICO

- **Pillow:** `Image.open("badge.bmp").save("badge.ico", sizes=[(16,16),(32,32),(48,48),(256,256)])` builds a multi-size icon in Python. Pillow ignores any size bigger than the original image.

### Problems with BMP files

Editable vector shapes and live type do not survive in a BMP, so thin strokes and small lettering that read well in a large preview can disappear when the picture is shrunk to icon size. Look at the icon at the size people will see.

Stretch a small icon over a high-DPI screen and it looks soft. Start from the largest clean picture you have, because a smaller bitmap is left at its size rather than scaled up.

An uncompressed BMP can also be bulky, so PNG or JPEG may be more practical when the picture is only being shared.

guide.title: About BMP files
guide.markdown:
### What is a BMP file?

BMP, the Windows Bitmap, is Microsoft's raster image family, used originally on Windows and OS/2. Windows 98 brought the fifth version in 1998, which is able to carry both an ICC profile and an alpha channel. The registered media type is image/bmp.

Pixels in a BMP are usually stored uncompressed, with run-length encoding as an optional lossless alternative. That makes the format simple to read and write, but it produces large files. Depth runs from 1 to 32 bits per pixel.

Most BMP files are Windows screen captures or system graphics; the format also serves plain Windows artwork and image exchange without compression. Microsoft controls the format, and the Library of Congress documents it among the formats it follows for preservation.

### Programs that open BMP files

Windows Paint, Windows Photos, Preview on macOS and GIMP all open BMP. Further programs, from the format's fact sheet:

**Windows, Mac and Linux**

- ImageMagick: reads BMP images, which the magick command can then write out as JPEG.
- XnView MP: BMP is among its supported image formats, and company use requires a license.

**Web**

- Firefox: shows BMP pictures inside web content.
- Google Chrome: BMP images are supported, per Mozilla's browser compatibility table.

### BMP and JPEG compared

- **Names and types**: .bmp is image/bmp. A JPEG may end in .jpg or in .jpeg.
- **Compression**: BMP commonly stores raw pixels, with lossless compression as an option. JPEG is lossy and designed for photographs.
- **Transparency**: BMP version 5 can store an alpha channel. JPEG has no alpha transparency.
- **Color depth**: BMP spans 1 to 32 bits per pixel. This page's JPEG comes from a browser canvas with 8 bits per channel.
- **Metadata**: a BMP can carry an ICC profile from version 5. This page does not copy it.
- **Typical use**: BMP serves simple Windows graphics and uncompressed image interchange. Web photographs, camera files, email attachments and shared photos are typically JPEGs.
- **Standard**: ISO/IEC 10918-1 specifies JPEG, a format that the Joint Photographic Experts Group created. Microsoft controls the BMP family.
- **Quality**: JPEG normally has an adjustable quality. This page fixes it at 0.85 and shows no slider.

The page asks your browser to decode the BMP with its own image decoder, then encodes a JPEG at quality 0.85 from a canvas. The picture goes through raw pixels with 8 bits per channel, so only the pixels survive: tags, an embedded ICC profile and any transparency are left behind. You get a single still picture, and the conversion runs on your own device with no server involved. The page imposes no size limit, and the BMP you started with stays as it was. A multi-file selection runs file after file, giving one JPEG per BMP, named like the BMP but ending .jpeg.

### Other ways to convert BMP to JPEG

- **GIMP on any desktop:** open the BMP, then pick File > Export As. A JPEG export dialog then lets you set the quality from 0 to 100, with a default of 85.
- **ImageMagick (command line):** run `magick scan-bitmap.bmp -quality 90 scan-photo.jpeg`. The -quality option takes 1 to 100, so you pick the quality yourself, which this page never lets you do.

### Problems with BMP files

- **The BMP takes up too much space**: an uncompressed BMP can be large, so PNG or JPEG may suit distribution better.
- **Transparency turned into something else**: JPEG cannot hold transparent pixels. Use the [BMP to PNG converter](/bmp-to-png/) if you must keep see-through areas.
- **A decode error from this page**: the browser could not read the file, which suggests damage or a file that is not truly a BMP.
- **Banding or blocks after converting**: JPEG is lossy, and here there is no way to raise the quality. Use the ImageMagick command above to pick a higher quality.
- **A different size from another editor**: the same quality number in two editors does not promise the same compression or look.
- **An old photo frame rejects a JPEG exported from GIMP**: some older photo frames reject progressive JPEG, so try an export with progressive mode disabled.
- **You need to edit it later**: a BMP does not preserve editable vector shapes or live typography, and JPEG has no editable layers either. Keep your project file.

### What is a BMP file?

The BMP family of raster images belongs to Microsoft and began on Windows and OS/2. Pixels are usually stored uncompressed, though lossless compression exists. - **Windows, Mac and Linux:** ImageMagick and XnView MP read BMP.
- **Web:** Mozilla Firefox and Google Chrome show BMP pictures inline.

- **Structure**: the SVG holds one `<image>` element with the picture embedded as a base64 PNG.
- **Size**: the embedded PNG matches the BMP's pixel dimensions, with no resizing or reduction.
- **Tracing**: none. Pixels do not become paths.
- **Transparency**: kept in the embedded PNG.
- **Metadata**: not written to the SVG.
- **Upload**: none, because the BMP stays on your device.
- **Original**: your BMP is not changed. You download a new SVG.
- **Display**: the SVG can be shown at any size, but a small BMP stays small and softens when stretched.
- **Several files**: choose many BMPs at once; each becomes its own SVG, with no ZIP.

### Other ways to convert BMP to SVG

- **Inkscape:** choose File > Import, pick the BMP and select Embed when the dialog asks whether to link or embed it. Its manual lists bmp among the formats it imports.
- **Potrace:** run `potrace -s -o outline.svg drawing.bmp` to trace a black-and-white bitmap into vector outlines instead of embedding it.

### Problems with BMP files

- **An uncompressed BMP is bulky**: PNG or JPEG may be more practical for distribution.
- **An old program rejects the header**: tools such as ImageMagick can write BMP3 or BMP2 output rather than the default BMP version.
- **A BMP has no editable vector shapes**: it also keeps no live typography, and an SVG wrapper does not add either.

guide.title: About CAF files
guide.markdown:
### What is a CAF file?

CAF, Core Audio Format, is a container Apple designed as a flexible home for audio. Core Audio support dates to OS X 10.4, with OS X 10.3 support through QuickTime 7. Where older containers use small size fields, CAF uses 64-bit offsets, so it has no 4 GB ceiling.

A CAF can hold compressed audio or uncompressed samples, with multiple channels and optional channel-layout information. A mandatory audio-description chunk identifies the stored audio encoding, and information and edit-comment chunks can carry descriptive text.

You meet CAF as audio on macOS and iOS, as long recordings and as sound effects in Apple apps. Many codecs fit inside it, so two CAF files can hold very different audio, and the format is also described as supporting metadata and markers. It is an Apple format.

### Programs that open CAF files

QuickTime Player, Apple Music, Logic Pro and Audacity open CAF files. The format's fact sheet adds these programs:

**Windows, Mac and Linux**

- FFmpeg: handles Core Audio Format containers in both directions.
- ffplay: uses FFmpeg demuxers and decoders to play supported CAF audio.

### CAF and WAV compared

- **Extensions and media types**: .caf for CAF; .wav for WAV, with audio/wav and audio/x-wav as common media-type labels.
- **Origin**: CAF is Apple's format. WAV comes from a Microsoft and IBM multimedia specification of August 1991.
- **Structure**: CAF uses 64-bit offsets. WAV is a RIFF-based wrapper for sound rather than one particular audio encoding.
- **Contents**: a CAF can hold compressed or uncompressed audio. WAV often holds linear PCM, though compressed encodings are possible as well.
- **Size limit**: CAF has no 4 GB limit. WAV has a 4 GB file size limit.
- **Metadata**: CAF has information and edit-comment chunks. What a WAV does with metadata varies, as INFO chunks and the Broadcast WAVE extensions store different details.
- **Typical use**: WAV serves audio recording and editing and professional sound production.

WAV, short for Waveform Audio File Format, is a RIFF-based sound wrapper described in the multimedia specification Microsoft and IBM published in August 1991. It usually holds uncompressed PCM audio, so files are large but exact. Broadcast WAVE carries production and preservation metadata. The Library of Congress names WAVE its recommendation for digital audio collections.

The conversion is a decode and rewrite. FFmpeg in your browser reads the CAF and writes 16-bit little-endian PCM into a WAV, dropping any video stream. The page passes no quality setting. No tag options are passed either; FFmpeg's defaults decide, and in a test the CAF's title and artist arrived in the WAV. The CAF stays unchanged, and the download takes its name with a .wav ending. A batch of CAF files runs in sequence and yields a separate WAV for each.

### Other ways to convert CAF to WAV

- **FFmpeg (Windows, Mac, Linux):** run `ffmpeg -i field-recording.caf -c:a pcm_s16le field-edit.wav`. 16-bit output can reduce the source depth.
- **Switch (Windows):** add the CAF, choose WAV as the output format, set the encoder options and an output folder, then click Convert. NCH lists CAF input and WAV output for Windows, Mac and Android versions of the program.

### Problems with CAF files

- **It opens but there is no sound**: opening the container does not guarantee that a system can decode the audio codec inside it.
- **The channel layout is not what you expected**: CAF can hold optional channel-layout information. Check the channel order in your editor after converting a multichannel recording.
- **A 24-bit recording loses depth**: the page writes 16-bit PCM, so a deeper CAF is reduced to 16 bits.
- **The WAV is much larger than expected**: the CAF held compressed audio, and PCM is uncompressed.
- **CAF notes are missing from the WAV**: information and edit-comment chunks in a CAF can carry descriptive text, but this page promises only what FFmpeg's defaults copy, such as global tags. Check the WAV in your editor if the notes matter.
- **A program cannot open the CAF at all**: FFmpeg reads and writes the Core Audio Format container, so it can turn the file into a WAV from the command line, and ffplay can play supported CAF audio.
- **A damaged or cut-short CAF**: such a file usually still converts, giving a shorter WAV, so compare its running time with the CAF.

guide.title: About CDR files
guide.markdown:
### What is a CDR file?

The default drawing format of CorelDRAW is CDR. Corel calls it a primarily vector format: instead of a grid of pixels, the drawing is kept as shapes, curves, text and effects, across multiple pages and layers. Bitmap content can sit inside a drawing next to vector effects, and the save options offer compression for bitmaps and for graphic objects.

Properties like a title and subject can be stored in a CDR, and fonts can be embedded where permissions and other restrictions allow. In the Save As dialog you can pick an earlier CDR version for compatibility, which matters because an older CorelDRAW may reject a drawing from a newer one.

You meet CDR files as logos, illustrations, signage and print design. CDR is a proprietary Corel format, and LibreOffice Draw and Inkscape read it through libcdr.

The target, JPEG, is a raster format with lossy compression, which the Joint Photographic Experts Group specified as ISO/IEC 10918-1. Web photographs, camera files, mailed attachments and shared pictures commonly use it, and its quality can be adjusted.

### Programs that open CDR files

**Windows, Mac and Linux**

- LibreOffice Draw: imports CDR through libcdr.
- Inkscape: uses libcdr for CDR input.

**Windows and Mac**

- CorelDRAW: opens its native drawings.

**Web**

- The web edition, CorelDRAW Web: documentation covers CDR support in compatible browsers; qualifying Graphics Suite subscribers and maintenance customers get access as a benefit.

### CDR and JPG compared

- **Names and types**: .cdr is CorelDRAW's native format. JPEG files end in .jpg or .jpeg, which mean the same thing.
- **Kind**: CDR is primarily vector. JPEG is a raster format designed for photographs, so shapes become pixels.
- **Compression**: JPEG is lossy, with no alpha transparency, so transparent pixels cannot survive a JPEG export.
- **Pages and layers**: a CDR can have multiple pages and layers. JPEG is one flat raster picture with no editable layers, so keep your CDR.
- **Support**: a JPEG is supported everywhere, and you can view it in Windows Photos, GIMP, Preview on macOS or a browser. A CDR opens in CorelDRAW, LibreOffice Draw and Inkscape.

This page cannot do the conversion. It runs in your browser, has no CDR reader of its own, and hands the file to the browser's image decoder, and the attempt ends with an 'Image decode failed.' error. Your file is not uploaded and is not changed. Pick one of the programs below, or ask whoever sent the drawing for a JPG. Once the drawing is a JPG its vector shapes are pixels, so pick the export size you need before saving, because enlarging the JPG afterwards cannot restore sharp edges.

LibreOffice Draw can export to any of the graphics formats BMP, EMF, EPS, GIF, JPEG, PNG, SVG, TIFF and WMF. CorelDRAW itself offers JPEG in its export dialog, with options for the current page or only the selected objects.

### Other ways to convert CDR to JPG

- **CorelDRAW on Windows or Mac:** open the drawing, choose File > Export, set Save as type to JPEG, type a file name, optionally tick Export this page only or Selected only, and click Export.
- **LibreOffice Draw on Windows, Mac or Linux:** open the CDR, then export it as JPEG. LibreOffice's guide lists JPEG among the graphics formats Draw exports and Corel Draw (*.cdr) among the formats it opens.

### Problems with CDR files

- **An older CorelDRAW will not open it**: the drawing was probably saved by a newer version. Ask for a copy saved in an earlier version, which the newer program offers.
- **The vectors are gone after PHOTO-PAINT**: that program turns an imported CDR into pixels. Keep the CDR for later vector edits.
- **Lettering changes on another computer**: fonts embed only where font permissions and other restrictions allow, so a drawing sent to someone else may not bring its fonts along.
- **This page stops with a decode message**: nothing here can read the format, so the file never reaches a JPG.
- **The JPG cuts off part of the design**: CorelDRAW can export only the selected objects or the current page, so check which option you picked before saving.
- **The JPG differs from what another program makes**: equal quality numbers in two programs do not mean equal compression or looks.
- **You only need a preview**: ask whoever made the drawing for a JPG.
