guide.title: About M4A files
guide.markdown:
### What is an M4A file?

M4A is the ending for MPEG-4 files that carry sound and no picture. The container is the same one MP4 video uses; the A just tells software to expect audio. Apple adopted the ending for unprotected music, and its media type is audio/mp4.

Inside, most M4A files hold AAC, the Advanced Audio Coding defined in MPEG-4 Part 3. AAC was designed to sound better than MP3 at the same bitrate, and it handles sample rates from 8 to 96 kHz and bitrates up to 512 kbps. Some M4A files hold Apple Lossless instead, which keeps the sound exactly but is much larger.

You meet M4A files in several places. Songs sold through iTunes used AAC. The iPhone's Voice Memos app saves its recordings as M4A, and audio ripped or imported with Apple's apps often ends up in the format too. Protected purchases use a sister ending, .m4p, and can't be played outside Apple's own software.

### Programs that open M4A files

**Windows**

- Media Player: Windows 11's built-in player handles M4A.
- iTunes: plays M4A and can make MP3 copies.
- VLC: plays it with its own decoders.

**Mac**

- Music: Apple's player and library, which can convert songs to MP3.
- QuickTime Player: plays a single file.

**Linux**

- VLC: plays M4A out of the box.
- Audacity: imports M4A for editing once its FFmpeg library is installed.

**Web**

- Every major browser plays AAC in an MP4 container, so an M4A plays when dragged into a tab.

**Mobile**

- iPhone and iPad: Music, Files and Voice Memos.
- Android: plays AAC in .m4a files on every version.

### M4A and MP3 compared

- **Extensions and media types**: .m4a with audio/mp4; .mp3 with audio/mpeg.
- **Codec**: M4A usually holds AAC and sometimes Apple Lossless. MP3 is one codec, MPEG-1 Audio Layer III, standardized as ISO/IEC 11172-3 in 1993 and extended by ISO/IEC 13818-3 in 1995.
- **Compression**: both AAC and MP3 are lossy and rely on a model of hearing to drop sounds listeners are unlikely to notice. AAC does more with fewer bits.
- **Range**: MP3 runs from 32 to 320 kbps at 32, 44.1 or 48 kHz. At 128 kbps an MP3 is about an eleventh the size of the same music on a CD.
- **Tags**: an M4A keeps titles and artwork in MPEG-4 metadata; an MP3 keeps them in ID3 blocks. This page leaves out cover art and doesn't promise that other tags come across, so check them after converting.
- **Support**: MP3 plays almost everywhere, from browsers to old car stereos. M4A plays in browsers and on phones but trips up some older hardware and software.
- **History**: MP3 was developed at Fraunhofer IIS from the late 1980s with partners in the MPEG audio group. Its patent licensing program ended on 23 April 2017.

What this page writes: an MP3 encoded with LAME at a constant 192 kbps. A minute of audio comes to about 1.4 MB, whatever the bitrate of the M4A you start from.

### Other ways to convert M4A to MP3

- **Apple Music (Mac)**: in Music > Settings > Files > Import Settings, set Import Using to MP3 Encoder, select the songs, then choose File > Convert > Create MP3 Version. Protected purchases can't be converted, and going from one lossy format to another costs some quality.
- **iTunes (Windows)**: choose Edit > Preferences, click General, then Import Settings, and set Import Using to MP3 Encoder. Select the songs and choose File > Convert > Create MP3 Version. Store purchases convert only if they are iTunes Plus songs.
- **VLC (Windows, Mac, Linux)**: open Media > Convert/Save, add the M4A with the Add button, pick an MP3 audio profile under Profile, choose where to save it as the Destination file, then press Start.
- **FFmpeg (command line)**: `ffmpeg -i input.m4a -c:a libmp3lame output.mp3`. MP3 encoding needs an FFmpeg build that includes the LAME library.

### Problems with M4A files

- **A car stereo or old player ignores the file**: it may not know AAC in MP4. An MP3 copy plays on nearly everything.
- **The file ends in .m4p**: it may be copy-protected, and a protected file can't be converted. An unprotected one converts with the [M4P to MP3 converter](/m4p-to-mp3/).
- **The MP3 is larger than the M4A**: the original used a low bitrate, which is common for voice recordings. That is normal, since this page always writes 192 kbps.
- **The artwork is missing**: cover art isn't carried into the MP3. Add it back in your player, for example with Get Info in Apple Music.
- **"FFmpeg failed with exit code N"**: the audio couldn't be decoded, perhaps because the file is cut short or isn't really an M4A. Play it first to check.
- **You plan to edit the audio**: every lossy save costs a little. The [M4A to WAV converter](/m4a-to-wav/) makes an uncompressed copy to work on, with no second lossy step.

faqs.answer: The page asks the LAME encoder for 192 kbit/s. MP3 can't reach that below a 32 kHz sample rate, and the sample rate isn't changed, so a source with a lower rate gets a lower bitrate in the MP3.

faqs.question: Will the MP3 sound better than the ringtone?
faqs.answer: No. Converting can't add quality, and both formats are lossy. Going from one lossy format to another adds a second lossy encoding step.

faqs.question: Can I use the MP3 as an iPhone ringtone?
faqs.answer: Not directly. An iPhone ringtone has to be an M4R, and Apple's GarageBand workflow limits a ringtone to 30 seconds. The MP3 is for players and apps that take MP3 files.

faqs.question: What is the difference between M4R and M4A?
faqs.answer: Both are MPEG-4 audio files. M4R is the ending for iPhone ringtones, while M4A marks MPEG-4 files carrying audio alone. This page reads the M4R and writes an MP3.

faqs.question: Will the MP3 keep the ringtone's tags?
faqs.answer: FFmpeg's defaults copy the input's global tags, such as title and artist, to an output that can hold them, and an MP3 holds them in ID3. If a field matters to you, check the MP3 in a tag editor.

faqs.question: Why won't my M4R convert?
faqs.answer: When FFmpeg cannot produce audio from the file, for example because there is no audio track, the result is the error "FFmpeg failed with exit code N" and no MP3. A damaged or cut-short ringtone often still converts, to a shorter MP3, so play the original first to see what it holds.

faqs.question: Is a 30-second ringtone converted whole?
faqs.answer: Yes. The page sets no length limit of its own, and the MP3 is made from the whole sound.

faqs.question: What happens to my original M4R?
faqs.answer: Nothing. The page doesn't change it. You download a new MP3 named after the ringtone, such as personal-tone.mp3.

faqs.question: Does the MP3 play everywhere?
faqs.answer: Nearly. Every major browser plays MP3, and the format is listed as playing on nearly every device.

guide.title: Understanding M4R for MP3 output
guide.markdown:
### What is an M4R file?

The M4R ending marks an iPhone ringtone. The contents are ordinary AAC in an MPEG-4 wrapper; only the ending sets it apart for iTunes and the iPhone. It sits in the MPEG-4 family, which keeps the container structure separate from the encoding of the tracks inside it. MediaInfo files the .m4r extension with the MPEG-4 formats, and NCH's WavePad manual calls M4R the ringtone type for iPhone. Like other MPEG-4 files, an M4R can carry track metadata beside the encoded sound. Audacity's documentation shows the other direction: its AAC export accepts .m4r as the filename of an MP4 ringtone.

Most people meet an M4R when they make a custom ringtone. Apple's GarageBand workflow on iPhone limits a ringtone to 30 seconds and offers to shorten a longer sound before it finishes. A dimmed source song in that workflow can mean it hasn't been downloaded to the phone.

### Programs that open M4R files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** MediaInfo shows the container and stream properties, and its format registry includes .m4r. It is not an audio player.
- **Windows:** WavePad reads and writes .m4r according to NCH's documentation, though it can't decode copy-protected input. NCH lists it on Windows but not on Mac, and links M4R output to the encoder options it shares with AAC and M4A.
- **Windows, Mac and mobile:** Switch, NCH's converter, accepts M4R input on Windows, Mac and Android, but excludes copy-protected files.
- **Mobile:** GarageBand for iPhone creates and installs custom ringtones from eligible audio.

### M4R and MP3 compared

- **Extensions and media types**: .m4r for ringtones; .mp3 for MP3, whose registered media type is audio/mpeg.
- **Standard**: The name MP3 abbreviates MPEG-1 Audio Layer III, which became ISO/IEC 11172-3 in 1993. Fraunhofer IIS and other MPEG audio group members built it, starting in the late 1980s.
- **Compression**: MP3 is lossy. It uses a model of human hearing to drop sound listeners are unlikely to notice. A 128 kbit/s MP3 occupies about one eleventh of the space that the same sound needs on a CD.
- **Audio coding**: an M4R holds AAC audio in an MPEG-4 container. AAC is a perceptual audio coding family standardized through MPEG, placed in MPEG-4 Part 3, and it is lossy. It was designed to sound better than MP3 at the same bitrate.
- **Sample rates and bitrates**: AAC covers sampling from 8 up to 96 kHz, with bitrates reaching 512 kbps. MP3 bitrates run from 32 to 320 kbps.
- **Tags**: titles and similar tags in an MP3 sit in ID3 structures kept apart from the audio.
- **Playback**: every major browser plays MP3. Patent licensing for the format ended on April 23, 2017.

Here, FFmpeg in your browser uses the LAME encoder and asks it for 192 kbit/s. Audio sampled under 32 kHz ends up with a smaller bitrate, since the page leaves the sample rate alone. Any video is dropped. The command passes no track options, so FFmpeg's defaults pick the stream and copy the input's title, artist and similar tags to the MP3.

MP3 keeps song titles and similar tags in ID3 structures, while the M4R keeps track metadata the MPEG-4 way. If a tag matters, check it in the MP3 and add it in a tag editor. A batch of ringtones is handled in sequence, and each MP3 is saved separately without a ZIP.

### Other ways to convert M4R to MP3

- **FFmpeg:** run `ffmpeg -i personal-tone.m4r -vn -c:a libmp3lame -b:a 192k personal-alert.mp3`. The `-vn` drops video, `libmp3lame` is FFmpeg's wrapper for the LAME encoder, and `-b:a` sets the audio bitrate in bits per second.

### Problems with M4R files

- **WavePad or Switch won't open it**: copy-protected input isn't decoded, so M4R support doesn't mean they can remove protection.
- **A ringtone is cut to 30 seconds**: if an export exceeds 30 seconds, GarageBand offers to shorten it before completing the ringtone.
- **A source song is dimmed in GarageBand**: it may be unavailable because it hasn't been downloaded to the iPhone.
- **A player says the file is unsupported**: open the file in MediaInfo, which inspects container and stream properties, to see what its tracks hold. Then convert it here to get an MP3.
- **This page reports "FFmpeg failed with exit code N"**: the file may have no audio track. Get the original ringtone again.

faqs.question: How do I turn an M4V into a MOV?
faqs.answer: Select your M4V file above, let the conversion finish, and then save the MOV. A batch is processed in order, and every result downloads separately.

faqs.question: Does the page re-encode or just copy the video?
faqs.answer: It re-encodes. Video becomes H.264 and audio becomes AAC, which makes the MOV a new generation with nothing passed through unchanged.

faqs.question: Will the MOV be smaller than the M4V?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily. The re-encode uses a fast setting that favors speed over compression, so the MOV can come out larger or smaller than the M4V.

faqs.question: Is the resolution kept?
faqs.answer: Up to 1920 px on the long side. Anything larger is shrunk to fit, and the even-side rule trims an odd width or height by one pixel.

faqs.question: Is the frame rate kept?
faqs.answer: A video at or below 30 fps keeps its rate. A faster one has frames dropped to cap it at 30 fps, and the clip is not slowed down.

faqs.question: Can I convert an M4V from the iTunes Store?
faqs.answer: FairPlay protection may be present on iTunes Store files, and this page does not strip it. Convert a file you made or are allowed to convert.

faqs.question: Why not just rename the M4V to MOV?
faqs.answer: They are different formats. A rename changes only the label, and a program that checks the data may refuse the file. Converting writes real MOV data.

faqs.question: What is the difference between M4V and MP4?
faqs.answer: Little beyond the ending and the codecs inside, since M4V can label an MPEG-4 container file. MOV is a different format from both.

faqs.question: Is interlaced M4V video fixed?
faqs.answer: Yes. Interlaced frames are deinterlaced before the H.264 encode, and progressive video passes through that step unchanged. The picture keeps its shape.

faqs.question: Is my M4V uploaded?
faqs.answer: No. FFmpeg runs in your browser, in its own worker, so the video stays on your device and the MOV is a new copy.

guide.title: Understanding M4V for MOV output
guide.markdown:
### What is an M4V file?

M4V is a label for an MPEG-4 container file. HandBrake treats the .m4v and .mp4 files it writes as one container, and it chooses the M4V ending for some jobs that combine chapters, subtitles and AC3 passthrough. In FFmpeg's source, the reader for MOV and MP4 files names .m4v among the endings it accepts. Inside, the MPEG-4 family keeps audio and video as separate tracks and stores metadata in boxes, so what plays depends on how each track was encoded.

You meet M4V files as exports from video software, as phone and tablet video, and as films or shows in iTunes and the Apple TV app. The ending doesn't reveal the codecs, which is why one M4V plays everywhere and another opens only in certain apps. Playback hangs on the encodings inside, so the first thing to learn about a stubborn file is its codecs, not its extension.

### Programs that open M4V files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** FFmpeg, the command-line tool, reads .m4v input explicitly in its MOV/MP4 reader. VLC media player supports MPEG-4 containers plus common MPEG-4 video and AAC audio.
- **Mac:** QuickTime Player opens M4V files and can export a movie as a MOV.

The MPEG-4 container family stores audio and video tracks, and M4V is one of its files.

### M4V and MOV compared

- **Names**: .m4v for M4V, and .mov or .qt for MOV, whose media type is video/quicktime.
- **Origin**: Apple created MOV as the QuickTime format in 1991 and shipped it for Windows in 1994. It later served as the basis of the MPEG-4 file format, yet MOV and MP4 stay separate and can't be swapped freely.
- **Structure**: a QuickTime file is assembled from objects named atoms, and software may skip any atom it can't read. The MPEG-4 family uses the same idea under the name boxes.
- **Contents**: H.264, ProRes or Motion JPEG video, with AAC or uncompressed PCM sound.
- **Reach**: browser support for MOV is patchy, and even Apple has largely moved to MP4. Mac screen recordings arrive as MOV files.

Here the video isn't copied across. FFmpeg in your browser rewrites it as H.264, using the ultrafast preset at CRF 32, and rewrites the sound as AAC at 96 kbps. The index goes at the front of the MOV so playback can start early. Anything over 1920 px on either side is scaled down, and frame rates beyond 30 fps are capped. Both sides are trimmed to even values, which costs an odd-sized picture one pixel, and interlaced frames get deinterlaced before encoding. Because it re-encodes, the MOV is a second generation of a lossy video. A fast preset trades compression for speed, so the file may be larger than a slow, careful encode would give. Your M4V is untouched; the result comes back as a separate file.

### Other ways to convert M4V to MOV

- **FFmpeg:** run `ffmpeg -i family-film.m4v -c:v libx264 -crf 21 -c:a aac -b:a 160k family-review.mov`. A lower CRF keeps more quality than this page does.

### Problems with M4V files

- **It won't play**: a codec the player lacks stops playback, even if the app knows the container. Try another player such as VLC.
- **Renaming didn't help**: a different suffix can't repair damage or add support for an unsupported encoding. Convert it instead.
- **It stops partway**: a normal MOV or MP4-family recording can be unreadable if writing ended early, and an interrupted export gives the same result. Export it again from the source project if you still have it.
- **The MOV is shorter than the M4V**: a damaged or cut-short M4V usually still produces a file: the MOV holds whatever the page managed to read and is shorter. Compare the lengths before deleting the original.
- **The MOV is bigger than expected**: the fast preset favors speed over compression, so a heavy source can stay heavy. Run FFmpeg yourself with a higher CRF number if you need a smaller file, and expect some loss of detail.
- **The MOV won't play in a web page**: browser support for MOV is limited, so check the result in a desktop player before you embed it.
- **It came from the iTunes Store**: such files may carry FairPlay DRM, which this page does not remove.

guide.title: Understanding MKV for WebM output
guide.markdown:
### What is an MKV file?

MKV is Matroska, a container for audio and video built on EBML, a binary format derived from XML. Its roots lie in a previous project, MCF. A single file can hold multiple video, audio and subtitle streams, and the design includes chapters and tags that describe the content. IANA lists video/matroska as its media type. MKV turns up in high-quality video collections and Blu-ray rips.

Matroska doesn't prescribe a compression method or a quality level. Two MKV files with the same ending can hold very different video and sound, so an MKV that plays in one app can fail in another that understands the container but lacks a decoder for what is inside. A file with several audio and subtitle streams can also start in the wrong language until you choose another track.

### Programs that open MKV files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** mpv offers desktop playback with a choice of audio and subtitle streams. ffplay comes with FFmpeg and its Matroska demuxer.
- **Mobile:** VLC for Android costs nothing, and its decoding depends on the media in the container. VLC for iOS can play most video formats, taken from local storage or from network sources.
- **Media servers:** Plex plays MKV libraries, and Windows Media Player opens MKV only with extra codecs installed.

Desktop players differ in how much they decode, so if one refuses a file, try another before you decide it is damaged.

### MKV and WebM compared

- **Relationship**: the WebM Project backs an open format for delivering media on the web, and its container is based on Matroska.
- **Codecs**: VP8 or VP9 for the picture, Vorbis or Opus for the sound. An MKV can hold far more.
- **Media types**: video/webm for video, audio/webm for sound only.
- **Typical uses**: MKV for video collections and rips; WebM for web video and browser screen recordings.
- **Terms**: the project releases the format technology royalty-free.
- **Playback**: browsers care about the codecs inside, not the .webm suffix. Safari 14.1 on macOS began playing WebM files that use VP8 or VP9 plus Vorbis.

Nothing is copied from the MKV here. FFmpeg in your browser rebuilds the video as VP8 with libvpx at CRF 40 in realtime mode and 4:2:0 color (yuv420p), and the sound as Vorbis at 64 kbps. These settings favor speed over compression, so expect lost detail and a bigger file than a slow encode would give. The frame keeps its size and speed, capped at 1920 px along the longer side and 30 frames per second. Both sides are trimmed to even values, so an odd-sized picture loses one pixel, and interlaced footage is deinterlaced first. Because the page doesn't map streams itself, FFmpeg's own defaults choose which video and audio tracks reach the WebM. The MKV itself isn't modified.

Keep the MKV when chapters, extra tracks or attachments matter. The WebM is a narrower copy meant for playback on the web, and it can't bring back anything the re-encode discarded.

### Other ways to convert MKV to WebM

- **FFmpeg:** run `ffmpeg -i lecture-archive.mkv -c:v libvpx-vp9 -crf 31 -c:a libopus lecture-browser.webm` for VP9 video and Opus audio. Here -c:v libvpx-vp9 picks VP9, -crf 31 sets the quality level and -c:a libopus picks the audio encoder.

### Problems with MKV files

- **No sound or the wrong language**: the player may have picked another audio or subtitle stream. mpv lets you switch tracks.
- **Seeking is slow or jumps**: missing or damaged cues make it harder to move around the file. Matroska stores cues apart from the media clusters, and a WebM with no cue index has the same trouble.
- **It opens but won't play**: recognizing the container doesn't mean the player can decode every codec inside. Try VLC.
- **The WebM looks softer than the MKV**: the encode favors speed, so fine detail and busy scenes lose the most. Use FFmpeg locally with a lower CRF number if quality matters more than speed.
- **A track is missing after conversion**: no stream-mapping options are passed, so play the WebM before you delete the MKV.
- **The WebM is shorter than the MKV**: with a damaged or cut-short MKV the conversion typically carries on and saves only the readable part, so check the running time before you delete anything.

guide.title: Understanding MOV for M4A output
guide.markdown:
### What is a MOV file?

A MOV is a movie in the QuickTime format, which Apple released in 1991 and which reached Windows in 1994. The files end in .mov or .qt and carry the media type video/quicktime. Inside, a QuickTime file is a set of objects called atoms, and a program can pass over any atom it doesn't understand. The video might be H.264, ProRes or Motion JPEG, and the sound might be AAC or uncompressed PCM. Screen recordings made on a Mac are saved as MOV, and iPhones record to it too; editors on macOS and professional pipelines use it as well.

The ending describes packaging, not quality or codecs, so one MOV can need decoders that another doesn't. QuickTime also fathered the MPEG-4 file format, though MOV and MP4 remain different and aren't interchangeable. Browsers support MOV only partly, and Apple now mostly uses MP4 itself. For this conversion what matters is the sound: a movie with no audio track can't give you a listenable file.

### Programs that open MOV files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** ffplay relies on FFmpeg's QuickTime demuxer plus the right decoders for the streams in the file. mpv gives desktop playback where the audio and subtitle tracks are yours to pick.
- **Windows and Mac:** Adobe Premiere imports MOV when a decoder for its contents is available.
- **Mac:** QuickTime Player plays the movie.
- **Mobile:** VLC for Android plays what its codecs cover, free of charge. VLC for iOS opens most movie formats from local and network storage.

### MOV and M4A compared

- **What it holds**: The M4A ending marks MPEG-4 files with audio and nothing else. Apple adopted it for music files without copy protection.
- **Codec**: almost every M4A holds AAC audio, a codec specified in MPEG-4 Part 3. AAC is lossy, and it was designed to beat MP3 at the same bitrate.
- **Range**: AAC supports 8 to 96 kHz sampling and up to 512 kbps. Songs sold through iTunes used it.
- **Reach**: all major browsers play AAC inside an MP4 container, and Android plays it in .m4a files on every release. Firefox may depend on system codecs for AAC.
- **Media type**: audio/mp4, against video/quicktime for the MOV.
- **Tracks**: the M4A carries one kind of track. Everything else in the movie, including any subtitles or extra video, stays in the MOV.

Here the soundtrack is not copied across. FFmpeg in your browser discards the video and turns the audio into AAC at 192 kbps, so the M4A is a new lossy generation of the sound, even if the MOV already held AAC. No stream-mapping options are passed, which means FFmpeg's defaults choose the audio track when a movie has several. A movie with no audio fails with the error "FFmpeg failed with exit code" and then the code itself. Files in a queue run one at a time, each saved separately. AAC is lossy and the sound is encoded again, so avoid converting the same recording back and forth. The page sets no limit on size or run time, and the MOV itself is never changed.

### Other ways to convert MOV to M4A

- **FFmpeg:** run `ffmpeg -i interview-camera.mov -vn -c:a aac -b:a 192k interview-listening.m4a`. The movie needs a valid audio stream.

### Problems with MOV files

- **The sound plays but the movie will not in a browser**: MOV support in browsers is partial, whereas every major browser plays AAC held in an MP4 container, which makes the M4A the safer file for a web page.
- **Your editor rejects it**: a QuickTime movie may use codecs the target editor doesn't have. Convert to a format it supports.
- **Renaming didn't help**: a new filename ending neither transcodes the video nor installs a missing decoder.
- **It broke after a crash**: a write cut short may leave an ordinary MOV unusable, though fragmented output recovers in a different way.
- **You need the picture too**: the M4A holds sound only, so keep the MOV if slides, gestures or on-screen text carry information the listener would miss.
- **The M4A is shorter than the movie**: a MOV that is damaged or cut short can still yield an M4A, but only for the stretch that could be read. Listen to the end before you delete the original.

guide.title: About MOV files
guide.markdown:
### What is a MOV file?

MOV is the QuickTime File Format. Apple introduced it with QuickTime in 1991 and brought QuickTime to Windows in 1994. Files end in .mov, or occasionally .qt, and are labeled video/quicktime. A MOV is a container: it holds separate tracks for video, sound, text and timecode, packed in building blocks called atoms. Software skips atoms it doesn't recognize, which let the format grow over the years without breaking older players.

The tracks inside can use many codecs. Common ones are H.264 or HEVC for everyday video, Apple ProRes and Motion JPEG for editing, and AAC or uncompressed PCM for sound. That range is why two MOV files can behave very differently: one plays everywhere, another needs special software.

You meet MOV files on Apple devices. The iPhone camera records them, a Mac saves screen recordings as MOV, and editing apps such as Final Cut Pro export them. They arrive by AirDrop, in cloud folders and as email attachments. Outside Apple's world they cause trouble, because browser support for MOV is limited, and Apple itself now generally uses MP4 for sharing.

### Programs that open MOV files

**Windows**

- VLC: plays most MOV files with its own codecs.
- Microsoft Clipchamp: imports a MOV and exports it as MP4.
- Adobe Premiere Pro: edits MOV footage, ProRes included.

**Mac**

- QuickTime Player: Apple's built-in player and the format's home.
- Final Cut Pro: Apple's editor, which reads and writes MOV.
- VLC: a fallback for unusual codecs.

**Linux**

- VLC and mpv: free players that read MOV.
- FFmpeg: converts or inspects MOV files from the terminal.

**Web**

- Safari plays MOV. Other browsers are inconsistent, which is the usual reason to convert.

**Mobile**

- iPhone and iPad: MOV is the camera's own format, so Photos and Files play it.
- Android: VLC for Android plays most MOV files.

### MOV and MP4 compared

- **Extensions and media types**: .mov or .qt with video/quicktime; .mp4 or .m4v with video/mp4.
- **Origins**: MOV is Apple's own format. MP4 is MPEG-4 Part 14, ISO/IEC 14496-14, published in 2003. Its structure, the ISO Base Media File Format, was derived from QuickTime, so MOV's atoms and MP4's boxes are the same idea, yet the two formats aren't interchangeable.
- **Typical codecs**: MOV is a common home for editing codecs such as ProRes. MP4 is the usual home of delivery codecs: H.264 video with AAC sound, and also HEVC, AV1, VP9, MP3 or Opus.
- **Playback**: every major browser plays MP4. MOV plays reliably only in Apple software and in players like VLC.
- **File size**: the container hardly matters. The codec and bitrate decide size, so the same H.264 video takes the same room as MOV or MP4.

What this page writes: H.264 video with x264's ultrafast preset at CRF 32, AAC sound at 96 kbps, the picture capped at 1920 px on its longer side and 30 frames a second, interlaced footage deinterlaced, and the index moved to the front of the file so playback can start before it has fully loaded.

### Other ways to convert MOV to MP4

- **VLC (Windows, Mac, Linux)**: choose Media > Convert/Save, click Add and pick the MOV, choose an MP4 profile from the Profile menu, set the Destination file and click Start. VLC's guide doesn't list its profiles by name.
- **FFmpeg (command line)**: `ffmpeg -i input.mov -c copy output.mp4` moves the tracks into an MP4 without re-encoding, so nothing is lost. It fails when the MOV holds a codec MP4 can't carry; leave out `-c copy` to re-encode instead.
- **Microsoft Clipchamp (Windows, web)**: add the MOV to a Clipchamp project, use the Export button in the top-right corner and pick a resolution. The video is re-encoded and saved as MP4.

### Problems with MOV files

- **It won't play in Chrome, Firefox or a Windows app**: convert it to MP4 here, or open it in VLC.
- **An iPhone video shows sound but no picture on Windows**: the video is probably HEVC, which Windows needs Microsoft's HEVC Video Extensions to play. The H.264 MP4 made here doesn't.
- **A website or form refuses the upload**: many accept MP4 but not MOV. Upload the converted file.
- **The MP4 looks softer than the MOV**: this page favors speed and size. Keep the MOV as your master copy.
- **It takes a long time**: a big MOV is decoded and encoded on your own device. Plug a laptop in and leave the tab open.
- **"FFmpeg failed with exit code N"**: the MOV couldn't be decoded, which usually means a damaged or half-copied file. Copy or download it again.
- **You need a GIF or just the sound**: use the [MOV to GIF converter](/mov-to-gif/) or the [MOV to MP3 converter](/mov-to-mp3/).

guide.title: About MOV files
guide.markdown:
### What is a MOV file?

MOV files are what QuickTime, Apple's media framework, writes. The format dates to 1991, and a Windows version arrived in 1994. Names end in .mov or .qt, and the registered media type is video/quicktime.

Inside, a MOV is assembled from objects called atoms. Software that meets an atom it does not recognize can skip it. The MPEG-4 file format started from QuickTime, though MOV and MP4 remain separate formats and neither substitutes for the other.

A MOV is only a container. Picture data may be H.264, ProRes or Motion JPEG; sound may be AAC or plain PCM. The extension never tells you which, so two .mov files can hold very different streams.

iPhone recordings and Mac screen recordings are the MOV files most people meet. Apple itself now generally uses MP4, and browser support for MOV is limited. Tracks for video, audio, text and timecode can sit together in a MOV, which professional video workflows use.

### Programs that open MOV files

**Windows, Mac and Linux:**

- ffplay plays MOV, because FFmpeg includes the format's demuxer.
- Desktop users get mpv, a player that lets you pick between audio streams.

**Windows and Mac:**

- Premiere from Adobe takes in MOV as long as it has the decoder the contents need.

**Mobile:**

- Android users can run VLC for Android, a free mobile media player.
- Most movie formats open in VLC for iOS, which reaches local and network media.

### MOV and MPEG compared

- **Origin**: MOV is Apple's QuickTime container. MPEG-2 grew out of compressed television delivery, and DVDs adopted it afterward.
- **Structure**: a MOV is a tree of atoms. In MPEG systems, coded picture, sound and data travel as streams, each elementary stream standing for a single coded component.
- **Video codecs**: MOV commonly holds H.264, ProRes or Motion JPEG. This page writes MPEG-2 video.
- **Audio**: AAC or PCM in a MOV, MP2 in the file produced here.
- **Typical use**: MOV for video editing on a Mac and for iPhone footage. MPEG files serve Video CDs, DVD video and older video downloads.
- **Packaging**: packetized elementary streams divide each coded component into packets. A file with the MPEG ending can hold a system stream or bare video. Sound and picture multiplexed into one file still keep separate codecs, so a player decodes both.
- **Extensions**: the endings .mpeg and .mpg both serve MPEG video, whose media type per the Library of Congress is video/mpeg.
- **Media type**: video/quicktime for MOV, with .mov or .qt as the extension.

The page does the conversion in your browser through FFmpeg. It decodes the MOV and writes new MPEG-2 video using a fixed quality scale of 6, then encodes MP2 sound at 96 kbps. Frames marked interlaced are deinterlaced, large pictures are cut down to fit 1920 pixels, and the rate stops at 30 frames per second. No DVD or VCD preset is applied.

You can add several MOV files. They run in the order added, and each MPEG arrives as its own file, not inside an archive. The page applies no size limit, and the time a long clip needs depends on your device. The original MOV is never altered, and nothing is uploaded.

There is no per-file quality or bitrate choice, because the MPEG settings are fixed. The methods below use FFmpeg presets instead.

### Other ways to convert MOV to MPEG

- **FFmpeg, PAL DVD preset:** run `ffmpeg -i interview.mov -target pal-dvd interview.mpeg`. The documentation says the -target option accepts vcd, svcd, dvd, dv and dv50, and allows a pal-, ntsc- or film- prefix on the type. All the format options (bitrate, codecs, buffer sizes) are then set automatically.
- **FFmpeg, preset without sound:** run `ffmpeg -i interview.mov -an -target pal-dvd silent.mpeg`. The -an option disables audio recording, so the result has only video.
- **FFmpeg, NTSC DVD clip:** run `ffmpeg -i interview.mov -target ntsc-dvd -t 30 first-30-seconds.mpeg`. As an output option, -t stops writing after the duration you give, here 30 seconds.

### Problems with MOV files

- **Codec missing in the editor**: QuickTime files can use codecs that the program you open them in does not include.
- **A renamed file**: editing the file name leaves the video as it was and adds no decoder.
- **An interrupted write**: a cut-short write can leave an ordinary MOV unusable, and fragmented output recovers in another way.

guide.title: About MOV files
guide.markdown:
### What is a MOV file?

Files ending in .mov are QuickTime movies. The Library of Congress dates the format to 1991 on Apple's side and to 1994 for Windows. Files can use the .qt extension too, and the media type is video/quicktime.

MOV is organized as a tree of atoms, and software is free to pass over ones it does not understand. MOV and MP4 share a root, because QuickTime served as the starting point of the MPEG-4 file format, yet each is its own format.

What the movie contains is a separate question. Video could be H.264, ProRes or Motion JPEG, and sound could be AAC or uncompressed PCM. The extension never tells you which.

You will find MOV files on a Mac, because screen recordings are saved in that format, and on iPhones. Browser support is limited and Apple now generally uses MP4 for its own work.

### Programs that open MOV files

**Windows, Mac and Linux:**

- mpv is a desktop player; you can switch between the audio and subtitle streams in a file.
- ffplay reads the container because FFmpeg includes its demuxer.

**Windows and Mac:**

- Adobe Premiere takes MOV files when it has the decoder for their codec.

**Mobile:**

- Android devices can use VLC for Android, a free player.
- VLC for iOS opens local and network media in most movie formats.

### MOV and MPG compared

- **Container versus family**: MOV is one specific container. MPG is an extension for MPEG-1 or MPEG-2 video and audio in an MPEG program stream.
- **Disc heritage**: the MPEG program stream was the standard for VCD and DVD video, while MOV is used for editing on a Mac and for iPhone recordings.
- **Number of tracks**: a MOV can hold video, audio, text and timecode tracks, whereas the MPG written here carries MPEG-2 video and MP2 sound.
- **Streams**: inside an MPEG file each coded component, such as the picture or the sound, travels as its own elementary stream.
- **Compression**: MPG is lossy, so converting a MOV into it means decoding the picture and compressing it again.
- **Audio**: a MOV may carry AAC or PCM. The MPG written here has MP2.
- **Uses**: MPG appears in Video CDs, DVD video, older downloads and broadcast capture.
- **Media type**: video/quicktime is MOV's registered type, and for MPEG video the Library of Congress gives video/mpeg.

This page decodes the MOV and builds a new MPG with FFmpeg inside your browser. The MPEG-2 picture is encoded with a fixed quality scale of 6, and the MP2 soundtrack runs at 96 kbps. Anything over 1920 pixels on its longer side is reduced, interlaced frames pass through a deinterlacing filter, and no more than 30 frames play each second. No DVD or VCD preset is used, so the result is a general MPEG-2 file, not a disc image.

Clips run in the order you add them, with a separate MPG saved for each. Everything runs in the tab, so nothing is uploaded, and how long a clip takes depends on your device. The page sets no limit on size, and your original MOV stays untouched.

Because these values are fixed, the page has neither a quality field nor a bitrate field. The presets below are the way to get a different set of options.

### Other ways to convert MOV to MPG

- **FFmpeg, VCD preset:** run `ffmpeg -i presentation.mov -target ntsc-vcd presentation.mpg`. FFmpeg's documentation gives `-target vcd` with a .mpg output as an example, and says all the codec and bitrate options are then set automatically.
- **FFmpeg, SVCD preset:** type `ffmpeg -i presentation.mov -target pal-svcd slides.mpg`. The type may be vcd, svcd, dvd, dv or dv50, with an optional pal-, ntsc- or film- prefix.
- **FFmpeg, film DVD preset:** use `ffmpeg -i presentation.mov -target film-dvd feature.mpg`. The film- prefix selects the film standard from the same list.

### Problems with MOV files

- **Missing codec in the destination**: a QuickTime file may use codecs that your editor lacks.
- **Only the name changed**: a new ending neither transcodes the video nor adds the decoder.
- **Unplayable after a crash**: an interrupted write can leave a regular MOV unusable, and fragmented output recovers differently.
- **Premiere or another editor will not take the MOV**: the editor may lack the decoder for what is inside, which is a different problem from the extension.

### What is a MOV file?

The MOV is the QuickTime movie format, introduced by Apple in 1991 and available on Windows since 1994. Files use the .mov or .qt ending, and video/quicktime is the registered media type. A file is organized in objects called atoms, which a program may skip when it doesn't recognize them. Inside you might find H.264, ProRes or Motion JPEG pictures paired with AAC or PCM sound.

iPhones record to MOV, macOS editors and professional pipelines use it, and Mac screen recordings arrive as MOV files. MPEG-4's file format was built on QuickTime, but the two aren't the same and can't stand in for each other. Browsers handle MOV poorly, and Apple itself now leans on MP4. A MOV says how its contents are packaged but not which codecs they use, so a file that edits smoothly in one program can be refused by another.

### Programs that open MOV files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** ffplay depends on FFmpeg's demuxer for the format and needs decoders for the actual streams. mpv is a desktop player with a track menu for audio and subtitles.
- **Windows and Mac:** Adobe Premiere imports MOV only when it has a matching decoder.
- **Mobile:** VLC for Android is free, with codec support deciding what plays. VLC for iOS reads most movie formats, local or network.

### MOV and WMV compared

- **Container**: WMV files are ASF containers that carry Windows Media content. ASF suits synchronized media that has to travel over a network, and it holds audio and video streams.
- **Delivery**: streams can come from a local disk or an HTTP server.
- **Compression**: WMV can use Windows Media Video 7, 8 or 9.
- **Media type**: the Library of Congress notes video/x-ms-wmv as commonly used, with no IANA registration.
- **Players**: VLC supports the ASF and WMV container and handles the 1, 2 and 9 generations of Windows Media Video. In FFmpeg's own list, the Windows Media Video 9 decoder is marked as not completely working, so support varies by player.

When a fixed hardware player or a legacy program asks for WMV, find out which codecs, maximum size and frame rate it accepts before converting. A new container can meet a delivery rule, but it can't make every movie run on every device. Keep the original MOV, since it may hold better quality than the copy.

The page re-encodes the video with FFmpeg in your browser and writes a WMV with FFmpeg's defaults for that container: MS-MPEG4 v3 video, which differs from Windows Media Video, plus WMA v2 sound at 128 kbit/s. Video keeps FFmpeg's default of 200 kbit/s, which leaves a busy scene looking soft. The frame is shrunk when it exceeds 1920 px on either side, the rate is held to 30 fps, and an odd-sized picture loses one pixel. Deinterlacing happens before encoding. Knowing the container isn't the same as having the video decoder, so an old player that opens some WMV files may still reject yours. Your MOV is not modified.

### Other ways to convert MOV to WMV

- **FFmpeg:** run `ffmpeg -i presentation-source.mov -b:v 1800k presentation-legacy.wmv`. FFmpeg guesses the WMV format from the ending and uses the -b:v option to set a higher video bitrate than this page does.

### Problems with MOV files

- **Your editor can't read it**: a QuickTime file can use codecs the destination editor never installed. Export a format it does handle.
- **Renaming didn't help**: swapping the ending doesn't transcode the video or add a missing decoder.
- **It stopped working after a crash**: an ordinary MOV may be unusable once writing was interrupted, whereas fragmented output has its own recovery behavior.
- **The WMV looks soft**: the page sets no video bitrate, so the default applies. A tool where you choose the bitrate, such as the FFmpeg line above, gives you control.
- **The player reads the file but shows nothing**: a program can parse the ASF wrapper without owning the decoder for what it holds, so a compatible reader is no promise of codec support.
- **The WMV won't play on the old device**: picture quality depends on the codec and compression settings, not the .wmv ending, so a legacy player can still refuse the result. Check what it supports.

guide.title: MP2 to MP3: format guide
guide.markdown:
### What is an MP2 file?

An MP2 file holds MPEG Audio Layer II, a lossy format with perceptual coding, defined in ISO/IEC 11172-3 and completed in 1992. ISO/IEC 13818-3 extends Layer II for MPEG-2. Its decoding complexity is low, and it is the predecessor of MP3, which is Layer III. You meet Layer II in digital radio, on DVD-Video soundtracks, in broadcast television and in Video CD production. The Library of Congress lists audio/mpeg as the media type for MP2 files.

An .mp2 audio file is not MPEG-2 video. People convert MP2 to MP3 for players, music libraries and apps that expect MP3.

### Programs that open MP2 files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** FFmpeg decodes and encodes MP2, ffplay plays it as well, and Audacity imports MP2 files natively.

### MP2 and MP3 compared

Both are lossy, so converting decodes Layer II and encodes Layer III, which adds a second round of loss. The MP3 here is made with LAME, which is asked for 192 kb/s. MP3, developed with major contributions from the Fraunhofer Society, grew into the most widely used format for music downloads. It supports constant or variable bitrate and ID3 tags, and it plays on nearly every device. The download is named after your MP2 with the .mp3 extension. A higher bitrate cannot recover sound the MP2 already left out. Editing the MP3 and exporting another MP3 adds a third lossy stage, so do your editing on the MP2 or a lossless copy.

### Other ways to convert MP2 to MP3

- **FFmpeg (command line):** enter `ffmpeg -i input.mp2 -c:a libmp3lame -b:a 192k output.mp3`.
- **Audacity (Windows, Mac, Linux):** bring the MP2 in with File > Import > Audio, then open File > Export Audio and select MP3.

### Problems with MP2 files

- **Mistaken for video**: Layer II is an audio coding, so a file that carries a picture is the wrong source here.
- **Lost detail**: lossy MP2 coding omits sound information, and decoding cannot recover what was discarded.
- **Surround needs speakers**: multichannel playback needs a suitable multichannel speaker arrangement.
- **A player offers no MP2 support**: convert the file to MP3.

MP3 to Transcript transcribes speech from audio or video files. Uploaded files are processed in your browser. If you paste a direct link to an audio or video file, the server fetches the file and streams it to your browser for transcription. YouTube, TikTok, SoundCloud, and other webpage links are not supported right now. The speech model downloads on first use and runs locally.

This tool is best for interviews, meetings, lectures, and voice notes. Larger files take longer to process and may use more memory.

**Why use this tool**

- Handles uploads or direct links to audio and video files.
- Creates a plain text transcript you can edit or share.
- Works with common audio and video formats.

faqs.question: Do my files get uploaded?
faqs.answer: Uploads are processed locally in your browser. If you paste a direct link to an audio or video file, the server fetches the file and streams it to your browser. The model files are downloaded when needed.

faqs.answer: Common audio and video formats like MP3, WAV, M4A, AAC, FLAC, OGG, OPUS, MP4, MOV, MKV, WEBM, AVI, and M4V.

faqs.question: Can I use YouTube or SoundCloud links?

faqs.question: Why is the first run slower?
faqs.answer: The speech model downloads the first time you run the tool. After that it is cached for faster use.

guide.title: Understanding MP3 for WebM output
guide.markdown:
### What is an MP3 file?

MP3, or MPEG-1 Audio Layer III, became a standard in 1993 as ISO/IEC 11172-3 and was extended in 1995 by ISO/IEC 13818-3. Fraunhofer IIS developed it from the late 1980s together with other people in the MPEG audio group. The format is lossy; it applies a model of hearing to drop sounds that listeners probably won't notice. At 128 kbit/s, an MP3 takes up roughly one eleventh of the space the same recording needs on a CD.

Supported bitrates run from 32 to 320 kbps, with sampling at 32, 44.1 or 48 kHz. Titles and other tags live in ID3 structures stored apart from the audio inside the file. Patent licensing for MP3 ended on April 23, 2017. Every major browser plays it, and audio/mpeg is its media type. Because the discarded sound can't be recovered, each new lossy encode removes a little more.

The file is most often a song, a podcast episode or a voice note. Because MP3 is not one of the codecs WebM allows, a request for WebM is really a request for a different audio package.

### Programs that open MP3 files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** Audacity imports MP3 audio into an editable project. ffplay uses FFmpeg's demuxer.
- **Web:** Firefox plays supported media directly. Chrome plays supported web audio, though the internal codec still matters.
- **Mobile:** VLC for Android is free, and codec support decides what plays. mpv for Android plays it too.

### MP3 and WebM compared

- **Purpose**: WebM comes from the WebM Project, which promotes an open format for the web. The container is built on Matroska.
- **Codecs**: VP8 or VP9 for video, Vorbis or Opus for sound. MP3 is not on that list, so the sound has to be encoded again.
- **Media types**: video/webm, and audio/webm for a file with no picture.
- **Typical uses**: WebM is used for video on the web, screen captures made in browsers and short animated clips, and the main browsers support it. MP3 serves songs, podcast episodes and voice notes.
- **Terms**: the project offers the format technology royalty-free.
- **Playback**: browsers look at the codecs inside, not the .webm ending. Safari gained support for VP8 or VP9 WebM with Vorbis in version 14.1 on macOS.

On this page, FFmpeg in your browser turns the sound of your MP3 into Vorbis at 64 kbps. Both formats are lossy, so the WebM is a second lossy generation, and you should keep the MP3 if quality matters. The original isn't changed, and the result is a separate download. Nothing in the page limits size or run time. Vorbis is one of the two audio codecs WebM defines, the other being Opus, so the output stays within the format's own choices. If you need Opus, run FFmpeg yourself with the command below. Play the WebM in the player you plan to use before you delete anything.

### Other ways to convert MP3 to WebM

- **FFmpeg:** run `ffmpeg -i spoken-note.mp3 -vn -c:a libopus -b:a 64k spoken-note-opus.webm` to write Opus instead of Vorbis. The -vn option turns off video, so an attached cover picture is left out.

### Problems with MP3 files

- **Import error**: a malformed MP3 can trigger an import error in an editor even though another player handles it.
- **Lost tags in an editor**: bringing several files into a single Audacity project can overwrite earlier tags with those of the last file.
- **Quality drops on re-export**: editing an MP3 and exporting a new MP3 adds a second lossy encoding stage. Export from the original source when you can.
- **A tag looks wrong**: titles and other tags sit in ID3 structures inside the MP3, so an editor that reads them differently can show different text. Check them in the player you will use.
- **Seeking is sluggish**: a missing cue index gives the player less direct location information, so jumping around in a WebM can be slower.
- **An old browser balks**: what an early Safari did says little about current releases, so try the WebM in the very browser you need.
- **Playback depends on the codec**: a player that recognizes the file may still lack the decoder, so try another one. VLC and mpv are free choices on Android.

faqs.question: What is 3GP format?
faqs.answer: 3GP (3rd Generation Partnership Project) is a multimedia container format designed for 3G mobile phones. It's optimized for mobile transmission and playback on devices with limited processing power and storage.

faqs.question: Why convert MP4 to 3GP?
faqs.answer: Convert to 3GP for compatibility with older mobile phones, feature phones, or when you need smaller file sizes for mobile transmission over limited bandwidth connections.

faqs.question: How does 3GP quality compare to MP4?
faqs.answer: 3GP typically offers lower quality than MP4 due to aggressive compression optimized for mobile networks. It uses smaller resolutions and lower bitrates to ensure smooth playback on mobile devices.

faqs.question: Can modern smartphones play 3GP files?
faqs.answer: Yes, most modern smartphones can play 3GP files, but they're primarily designed for older mobile devices. For modern phones, MP4 provides better quality and is the preferred format.

faqs.question: What are typical 3GP file sizes?
faqs.answer: 3GP files are very small compared to MP4 - often 10-20MB for a full-length video that might be 100MB+ in MP4. This makes them ideal for sharing over mobile networks with data limitations.

faqs.question: Is the conversion process secure?
faqs.answer: Absolutely secure! All 3GP conversion happens locally in your browser. Your video files never leave your device, ensuring complete privacy during the conversion process.

guide.title: About MP4 files
guide.markdown:
### What is an MP4 file?

MP4 debuted in 2003 as MPEG-4 Part 14, which carries the number ISO/IEC 14496-14. The ISO Base Media File Format supplies the layout, taking over the box-in-box design that Apple's QuickTime atoms pioneered.

Think of MP4 as packaging and not as a codec. The common contents are H.264 pictures with AAC sound, but AV1, VP9, MP3 and Opus fit too. Video files take .mp4 or .m4v, and MPEG-4 files with sound only often take .m4a. Registered media types: video/mp4 and audio/mp4.

All major browsers play MP4. On Android, HEVC video inside it works from version 5.0.

### Programs that open MP4 files

**Windows, Mac and Linux:**

- Desktop playback in mpv comes with selectable audio streams.
- Playing MP4 through ffplay works because FFmpeg has the demuxer.

**Windows and Mac:**

- Importing MP4 into Adobe Premiere succeeds when the decoder for its contents is available.

**Web:**

- Firefox plays supported media directly, although AAC and H.264 can depend on codecs in the system.
- Chrome plays the MP4 pairings it supports, and the inner codec stays decisive.

**Mobile:**

- Free to use, VLC for Android decodes according to what the container holds.
- A mobile player for most movie formats is VLC for iOS, which also reaches network media.

### MP4 and AAC compared

- **Kind of thing**: MP4 is a container, and AAC is a codec, and MPEG covers it in Part 7 of the MPEG-2 standard as well as in Part 3 of MPEG-4.
- **Contents**: an MP4 can carry pictures and sound. A .aac file is a single stream of audio.
- **Wrapper**: a standalone .aac file commonly carries ADTS framing, while AAC inside an MP4 sits in boxes.
- **Quality goal**: As a lossy codec, AAC aims at better sound than MP3 for an equal bitrate.
- **Use**: Streaming audio and end-user delivery are typical uses, and its media type is audio/aac.
- **Profiles**: they include LC, HE-AAC and HE-AAC v2.
- **Range**: Sample rates in AAC span 8 to 96 kHz, and bitrates reach 512 kbps.
- **M4A**: Unprotected music files from Apple took the .m4a extension, and most contain AAC audio.

This page decodes the MP4 in your browser with FFmpeg and discards the video. The sound goes through FFmpeg's AAC encoder at 192 kbps and is saved as a .aac file. The page has no bitrate field, no trimming and no tag editing, and it does not copy the original stream.

Add several MP4 files and they run in sequence, each producing a separate .aac. An MP4 without sound has nothing to extract. If FFmpeg gives up on a file, you see a message that begins "FFmpeg failed with exit code". Nothing is uploaded, no size limit applies, and the original MP4 stays as it was.

Because AAC is already compressed, encoding it again is a second pass of lossy compression. The copy method below avoids that when the audio in your MP4 is AAC.

### Other ways to convert MP4 to AAC

- **FFmpeg, re-encode:** run `ffmpeg -i recording.mp4 -vn -c:a aac -b:a 192k recording.aac`. With -vn the video is omitted, while -b:a fixes the audio bitrate.
- **FFmpeg, copy the stream:** type `ffmpeg -i interview.mp4 -vn -c:a copy -f adts extracted.aac`. Nothing is re-encoded, so it fits an MP4 whose sound is already AAC, and the adts muxer accepts a single AAC stream.
- **FFmpeg, choose an audio track:** use `ffmpeg -i lecture.mp4 -map 0:a:1 -c:a aac -b:a 192k second-track.aac`. In the specifier 0:a:1, the 0 is the first input and a:1 is the audio stream with index 1, counted from zero; the command fails when the file has fewer audio streams.

### Problems with MP4 files

- **No decoder for the contents**: a container that is supported does not guarantee a decoder for the sound or picture in it.
- **No audio track**: an audio editor has nothing to import from an MP4 that carries no sound.
- **Unfinished recording**: an ordinary MP4 holds its packet metadata in one place, so a write that was cut off can leave an unplayable file.
- **Variant mismatch**: software built for MPEG-2 AAC may fail on MPEG-4 AAC variants.
- **Renamed ending**: changing .aac to .m4a does not swap ADTS framing for an MP4 wrapper.

guide.title: About MP4 and DivX
guide.markdown:
### What is an MP4 file?

MP4 is formally MPEG-4 Part 14, or ISO/IEC 14496-14, and dates from 2003. Under the hood it follows the ISO Base Media File Format; that standard comes out of Apple's QuickTime format, and stores its data in nested boxes (QuickTime's word was atoms).

The file wraps streams instead of fixing one codec. H.264 with AAC is the common combination, though AV1, VP9, MP3 and Opus can sit inside too. Both .mp4 and .m4v mark video. Registered media types: video/mp4 and audio/mp4. On Android, HEVC video inside an MP4 plays from version 5.0 on.

### Programs that open MP4 files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** mpv plays MP4 on the desktop.
- **Windows and Mac:** Adobe Premiere imports MP4.
- **Web:** Firefox and Chrome play MP4 directly.
- **Mobile:** VLC for Android plays MP4, and so does VLC for iOS.

### MP4 and DivX compared

- **Container**: MP4 is MPEG-4 Part 14. DivX is a brand of video codec and container software from DivX, Inc., and its files are usually AVI.
- **Video**: MP4 commonly carries H.264, H.265 or AV1. Early DivX versions were MPEG-4 Part 2 video, and later versions added H.264. This page writes MPEG-4 Part 2 video.
- **Audio**: this page writes MP3 at 96 kbps.
- **Extras**: Menus and chapter points come from DivX authoring, and a DivX movie can hold more than one audio track. This page adds no menu.
- **Devices**: DivX certification profiles distinguish what a device can play, and advanced menus, chapters and tracks depend on the receiving device's profile.

The .divx extension is one of the formats DivX Player lists. The converter names your download with that extension.

### Other ways to convert MP4 to DivX

- **FFmpeg (command line):** run `ffmpeg -i source_movie.mp4 -c:v mpeg4 -vtag DIVX -c:a libmp3lame legacy_movie.avi`. The video is MPEG-4 with the DIVX tag, as in the converter above, and the audio is MP3.

### Problems with MP4 files

- **A player shows no picture or no sound**: a player that opens the container also needs a decoder for what each stream holds.
- **A cut-off recording won't play**: a normal MP4 stores its packet metadata in one place, so an early stop can leave the file unplayable.

guide.title: About MP4 files
guide.markdown:
### What is an MP4 file?

MP4 is MPEG-4 Part 14, ISO/IEC 14496-14, first published in 2003. It is a container: it wraps video, audio and other tracks rather than defining how they are compressed. MP4 is built on the ISO Base Media File Format, which grew out of Apple's QuickTime, and stores everything in nested boxes, the structures QuickTime calls atoms.

Most MP4 files pair H.264 video with AAC audio, but the format also carries AV1, VP9 and HEVC video and MP3 or Opus audio. Phones, cameras, screen recorders and video sites all produce it: Android's built-in screen recorder saves MP4, for example, while a Mac saves screen recordings as .mov. A GIF made from an MP4 plays where a video can't: in a chat thread, a help article, a README or a forum that takes images but not video.

### Programs that open MP4 files

**Windows**

- Media Player: Windows' built-in player. HEVC video needs Microsoft's HEVC Video Extensions.
- VLC: free player with its own codecs.
- Clipchamp: Microsoft's video editor, which also exports short clips as GIF.

**Mac**

- QuickTime Player: Apple's built-in player, which can also trim a clip.
- VLC: plays MP4s whose codecs QuickTime lacks.

**Linux**

- VLC and mpv: free players for nearly any codec.

**Web**

- Every major browser plays MP4 with H.264 video. Support for other codecs inside it varies.

**Mobile**

- iPhone and iPad: Photos and Files play MP4.
- Android: the gallery and video apps, with HEVC in MP4 from Android 5.0.

### MP4 and GIF compared

- **Extensions and media types**: .mp4, or .m4v for some video files, with video/mp4; .gif with image/gif.
- **What's inside**: an MP4 holds video and audio tracks. A GIF holds a series of palette images, with the delay between them set in hundredths of a second.
- **Color**: video can show millions of colors. Each GIF image uses at most 256.
- **Compression**: video codecs predict motion from frame to frame. GIF compresses each image on its own, losslessly, with LZW.
- **Transparency**: a GIF can mark one palette color as fully transparent, with no partial transparency.
- **Sound**: an MP4 can have audio. A GIF has none.
- **History**: CompuServe introduced GIF in 1987, and GIF89a, dated July 1990, added transparency, frame timing and application data.

What this converter does: it deinterlaces interlaced video, takes 15 frames per second, and scales the picture so its longer side is at most 480 pixels, with even sides. It then builds one palette from the clip, maps every frame to it, and sets the GIF to loop forever. The sound is left behind.

### Other ways to convert MP4 to GIF

- **Adobe Photoshop (Windows, Mac)**: choose File > Import > Video Frames to Layers, make a frame animation from the layers in Window > Timeline, then save with File > Export > Save for Web (Legacy) as a GIF. It needs a compatible codec, and a long video may not import in full.
- **Microsoft Clipchamp (Windows, web)**: add the video to a project, click Export at the top right and choose GIF. The option appears only for videos of 15 seconds or less.
- **FFmpeg (command line)**: run `ffmpeg -i input.mp4 output.gif`. GIF frame delays can't be shorter than a hundredth of a second, and the output loops forever unless `-loop` says otherwise. This page runs FFmpeg too, with a palette built from your clip.

### Problems with MP4 files

- **It won't play on Windows**: an HEVC video needs the HEVC Video Extensions. VLC plays it without them.
- **"FFmpeg failed with exit code N"**: FFmpeg couldn't read the video, for example because the file is damaged. Try another copy.
- **The GIF is too big to post**: GIF size grows with every second. Trim the video before converting.
- **Colors band or speckle**: 256 colors can't cover smooth gradients, so skies and shadows show steps or dots.
- **A long video takes ages**: everything runs on your device with no time limit, so a long clip takes longer.
- **Your video is a .mov**: use the [MOV to GIF converter](/mov-to-gif/).

guide.title: Understanding MP4 and M4R
guide.markdown:
### What is an MP4 file?

ISO/IEC 14496-14 (MPEG-4 Part 14), published in 2003, defines the MP4 container. It holds separate tracks for video, audio, subtitles and metadata rather than being a codec itself. Most files pair H.264 pictures with AAC sound, and other codecs such as AV1, VP9, MP3 or Opus are allowed. The file is made of nested boxes, the idea QuickTime calls atoms. Registered media types: video/mp4 and audio/mp4. A container is a wrapper: it organizes the tracks, and codecs such as H.264 and AAC compress what each track holds.

The MP4 design is derived from the ISO Base Media File Format, which counts Apple's QuickTime among its ancestors. QuickTime came first, and the MPEG-4 file format took it as its basis. Files with pictures usually end in .mp4 or .m4v; audio-only MPEG-4 is commonly saved as .m4a.

You meet MP4 as phone and camera recordings, downloaded clips and almost every video on the web, since every major browser plays it. For a ringtone only one track matters: the audio. An MP4 with a picture but no sound has nothing to give an audio editor.

### Programs that open MP4 files

**Windows, Mac and Linux:**

- ffplay, the player that ships with FFmpeg, includes the MP4 demuxer.
- mpv is a desktop player where you choose the audio and subtitle stream.

**Windows and Mac:**

- Adobe Premiere imports MP4 files into a project.

**Web:**

- Firefox opens MP4 files directly in a tab.
- Chrome opens MP4 files directly too.

**Mobile:**

- VLC, a free media player, has versions for Android and for iOS that open most movie formats.

### MP4 and M4R compared

- **Extensions**: .mp4 and .m4r. An M4R carries AAC sound in an MPEG-4 file, and the ending is what makes iTunes and the iPhone offer it as a ringtone.
- **Content**: an MP4 holds picture and sound. An M4R holds sound only.
- **Container**: both are MPEG-4 family containers.
- **Pictures**: the conversion disables video output, so no picture track reaches the M4R.
- **Compression**: both usually hold lossy codecs. The MP4's own audio is often already AAC, so this conversion encodes lossy sound a second time.

The conversion runs FFmpeg inside your browser tab and writes the audio as AAC at 192 kbps in an iPod-style MPEG-4 file, with the video dropped. It does not cut anything, so the M4R is as long as the soundtrack. Putting the ringtone on a phone is a separate step.

### Other ways to convert MP4 to M4R

- **FFmpeg:** run `ffmpeg -i clip.mp4 -b:a 192k -c:a aac -vn -f ipod tone.m4r`. The flags choose AAC at 192 kbps, drop the video and name the container, which FFmpeg's format documentation describes as MPEG-4 audio limited to audio streams.
- **GarageBand for iPhone:** first extract a sound file, for example `ffmpeg -i clip.mp4 -vn sound.wav`. In GarageBand tap the Loops Browser button, then Files, then Browse items from the Files app, and drag the file all the way to the left in Tracks view. Tap Share, then Ringtone, name it and tap Export.
- **WavePad (Windows):** extract a WAV the same way, open it in WavePad and save the result as M4R. NCH's format table lists WAV among the formats WavePad opens and M4R among those it saves on Windows, and not on Mac.

### Problems with MP4 files

- **No audio comes out**: the MP4 has no sound track. Play the original first. A silent screen recording has no sound to pull out, and the page then reports a failed conversion.
- **The video won't play anywhere**: container support doesn't guarantee a decoder for the video inside. Try a different player.
- **The file stops partway or won't open**: a recording that was cut off while being written may not play at all. Capture or download it again.
- **The ringtone is too long**: Apple says ringtones can be up to 30 seconds, and GarageBand offers to shorten a longer one. This page does not trim, so cut the sound first or let GarageBand do it.
- **The audio isn't AAC**: an MP4 can hold MP3 or Opus sound instead. That makes no difference here, because the converter encodes the sound as AAC whatever the MP4 held.
- **A phone won't play the video**: Android supports HEVC video inside MP4 files starting with version 5.0.

guide.title: Understanding MP4 and M4V
guide.markdown:
### What is an MP4 file?

The MP4 format, MPEG-4 Part 14 (ISO/IEC 14496-14), appeared in 2003 as a container. A container is a wrapper that holds tracks and says nothing about how they are compressed: an MP4 can carry H.264, H.265 or AV1 video next to AAC, MP3 or Opus sound, with subtitles and chapters beside them. Inside, the file is a tree of boxes, which QuickTime calls atoms. That standard descends via the ISO Base Media File Format from Apple's QuickTime.

Almost everything you record or download as video is an MP4: phone clips, camera footage, saved web video. Every major browser plays it, and its registered media types are video/mp4 and audio/mp4. Android has played HEVC video in MP4 files since version 5.0. Because it is a container, whether a given MP4 plays depends on the codecs inside as much as on the .mp4 ending.

### Programs that open MP4 files

**Windows, Mac and Linux:**

- mpv plays MP4 on the desktop and lets you choose the audio and subtitle stream.
- ffplay, the player included with FFmpeg, reads the MP4 format.

**Windows and Mac:**

- Adobe Premiere imports MP4 into editing projects.

**Web:**

- Chrome and Firefox play MP4 directly in the page.

**Mobile:**

- VLC plays MP4 on Android phones and tablets, and its iOS version handles most movie formats on iPhone and iPad.

### MP4 and M4V compared

- **Extensions**: .mp4 and .m4v. MDN lists both as extensions for video MPEG-4 files, and notes that audio-only MPEG-4 files often use .m4a.
- **Maker**: MP4 is an ISO standard. M4V is Apple's name for a very close relative, found in iTunes and on Apple TV.
- **Container**: HandBrake's documentation calls the two the exact same file apart from the extension.
- **Copy protection**: iTunes Store M4V files can be protected with FairPlay. An MP4 made here carries no such protection.
- **Codecs**: usually H.264 video with AAC audio in both.

Nothing is re-encoded here. FFmpeg lifts the existing video and audio streams out and sets them in a fresh MPEG-4 file with the .m4v ending, and the picture keeps the MP4's frame size and rate. The 1920 px and 30 fps limits that other video pages apply don't apply here, because the streams are copied instead of re-encoded. Since no compression is repeated, no quality is lost, and the job is mostly rewriting the container. The page puts no cap on size; a long file only takes your device longer, and you can choose several MP4 files at once. The M4V plays only where the player supports the codecs inside, just as the MP4 did.

### Other ways to convert MP4 to M4V

- **FFmpeg:** run `ffmpeg -i source.mp4 -c copy -f mp4 output.m4v`. The -c copy option is FFmpeg's stream copy, which passes the video and audio through without re-encoding, and -f mp4 sets the output container to MP4 under the .m4v name.
- **Rename a copy:** The HandBrake page calls the two the same file with a different extension, so you can copy the file and change .mp4 to .m4v. It adds that QuickTime and QuickTime-based apps can't play an MP4 with AC3 pass-through, subtitles or chapters enabled unless the ending is .m4v, which is a reason to rename a copy for those players.

### Problems with MP4 files

- **The video shows nothing or the sound is missing**: the container opens, yet a decoder for something inside is missing. Container support alone doesn't guarantee a decoder for the video or sound in it, so try another player.
- **The codecs inside suit one device and not another**: a new ending doesn't change what a player can decode. This page copies the codecs unchanged, so re-encode the video in another program if a device refuses them.
- **The picture plays but the sound doesn't, or the reverse**: an MP4 holds separate tracks, and a player may have a decoder for only one of them. The M4V behaves the way the MP4 did, because both tracks are copied as they are.
- **Renaming didn't fix it**: changing the ending can't repair a damaged file or an unsupported encoding.
- **The file is cut short or won't open**: an MP4 normally keeps its index data together, so a recording stopped mid-write may stay unplayable. Capture or download it again.

guide.title: MP4 to MJPEG: format guide
guide.markdown:
### What is an MP4 file?

MP4 is MPEG-4 Part 14 (ISO/IEC 14496-14), a container for video, audio and metadata. H.264 video with AAC audio is the pairing you will meet most. MP4 turns up as online video and streams, as phone and camera recordings, and as files passed between people.

Because MP4 is a container, the codec inside decides what a player needs.

### Programs that open MP4 files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** ffplay plays MP4, and mpv plays it on the desktop.
- **Windows and Mac:** Adobe Premiere imports MP4 once the decoder it needs is present.
- **Web:** Firefox plays supported media directly, and Chrome plays supported MP4 combinations.
- **Mobile:** VLC on Android (VLC for Android) and on iPhone (VLC for iOS) both play MP4, and decoding depends on the media inside.

### MP4 and MJPEG compared

Motion JPEG codes a video as a succession of individually JPEG-coded images, with no compression between frames, so its files usually come out larger than H.264. It is a video encoding rather than a container: AVI files commonly mark it with the MJPG FourCC, and QuickTime is another wrapper. This page stores the Motion JPEG in an AVI wrapper, turns the sound into 16-bit PCM and limits the picture to 1920 px on the longer side and the frame rate to 30 fps. Frames flagged as interlaced are deinterlaced first. MJPEG turns up in webcams and IP cameras, video editing and digital cameras' video modes. The OpenDML extension to AVI defines a profile for storing MJPEG, and production workflows may edit MJPEG and then use another encoding for delivery.

### Other ways to convert MP4 to MJPEG

- **FFmpeg (command line):** enter `ffmpeg -i input.mp4 -c:v mjpeg -q:v 5 output.avi`. It applies none of this page's size or frame-rate limits.

### Problems with MP4 files

- **No decoder for what is inside**: a container can be supported while the decoder for its video or sound is missing.
- **An unfinished file will not play**: an MP4 interrupted while being written can be unplayable, since its packet metadata is stored together.
- **No audio track to extract**: audio editors need an audio track, and an MP4 without one has none to give.

guide.title: About MP4 and MP2 files
guide.markdown:
### What is an MP4 file?

An MP4 keeps a video's picture and sound as separate tracks inside one wrapper. Standards bodies call the wrapper MPEG-4 Part 14, numbered 14496-14 by ISO and IEC, and it appeared in 2003. Apple's QuickTime is the ancestor, with the ISO Base Media File Format in between, and the file itself is a tree of nested boxes (QuickTime's term is atoms).

MP4 is a container, so the extension says nothing about how the contents were compressed. The common contents are H.264 pictures and AAC sound, though AV1, VP9, MP3 or Opus can sit inside too. Video files take .mp4 or .m4v, audio-only MPEG-4 files frequently take .m4a, and the media types on record are video/mp4 and audio/mp4. You come across MP4 in online video, phone and camera recordings, and clips people share. For this pair, the converter takes the soundtrack and writes it again as MP2.

### Programs that open MP4 files

**Windows, plus Mac**

- Premiere, from Adobe, will import an MP4 provided the decoder for its contents is present.

**Windows, Mac and Linux**

- ffplay plays MP4 through FFmpeg's MP4 demuxer.
- mpv is a desktop player that offers a choice of audio and subtitle tracks while an MP4 plays.

**Web**

- Firefox plays MP4 in the page, but whether AAC and H.264 work can hinge on codecs the system supplies.
- Chrome plays supported web audio and MP4 combinations, and the codec inside still matters.

**Mobile**

- VLC for Android is a free mobile player, and its decoding follows whatever codecs the MP4 holds; VLC for iOS opens most movie formats, whether stored on the phone or reached over a network.

### MP4 and MP2 compared

- **Names and types**: .mp4 goes with video/mp4 and audio/mp4, while .mp2 goes with audio/mpeg.
- **What a file holds**: a single MP4 may combine video, audio, subtitles and chapters, while an MP2 file holds audio only.
- **Compression**: MP2 is MPEG-1 Audio Layer II, specified in ISO/IEC 11172-3 and finalized in 1992. It is lossy and perceptual, it needs little decoding work, and it came before MP3, which is Layer III. ISO/IEC 13818-3 extends Layer II for MPEG-2.
- **Where it is used**: digital radio and television broadcasting, Video CD production and DVD-Video soundtracks.
- **The name trap**: the MP2 produced here is MPEG audio Layer II, and it is unrelated to MPEG-2 video files.

Here the picture is left out and the sound is encoded again. FFmpeg writes MPEG-1 Layer II at 192 kbps, whatever codec the MP4's audio used. MP2's lossy coding omits sound information that decoding cannot recover, so the conversion cannot bring back detail the MP4's audio did not have.

### Other ways to convert MP4 to MP2

- **FFmpeg (Windows, Mac, Linux):** run `ffmpeg -i video.mp4 -vn -c:a mp2 -b:a 192k soundtrack.mp2`. The `-vn` option disables video, and FFmpeg's documentation lists MP2 among the audio codecs it can encode. This is the same single encode the page runs.
- **Audacity (Windows, Mac, Linux):** Audacity imports MP4 audio only with its optional FFmpeg library installed. Import the file, choose File > Export Audio and select MP2 in the Format list. The bit rate runs from 16 to 384 kbps, with 160 kbps as the default.
- **TwoLAME with FFmpeg (command line):** run `ffmpeg -i video.mp4 -c:a pcm_s16le -vn extracted.wav`, then `twolame -b 192 extracted.wav soundtrack.mp2`. It takes two steps because TwoLAME reads sound files through libsndfile, and `-b` sets the total bitrate in kbps.

Audacity suits you when you want a bitrate other than 192 kbps. The TwoLAME route uses a dedicated Layer II encoder, at the cost of a large intermediate WAV file, since WAV usually holds uncompressed audio.

### Problems with MP4 files

- **No sound to extract**: an MP4 without audio cannot give an audio editor a track, and this page fails with an FFmpeg exit-code error. Play the video and listen for sound first.
- **No decoder for what is inside**: a player that accepts the MP4 wrapper may still lack a decoder for the video or sound it carries. Identify the codecs before blaming the player.
- **The file stops partway**: ordinary MP4 files store their packet metadata in one place, which means a recording or download cut short can leave something unplayable. Record or fetch it once more.
- **The MP4 holds several audio tracks**: some players let you choose a track, and mpv shows the audio streams a file has. Check which track you want before converting.
