guide.title: About TTF files
guide.markdown:
### What is a TTF file?

A TTF file holds a TrueType font. Apple developed TrueType and licensed the technology to Microsoft, and System 7 shipped with it in May 1991. A TrueType font describes scalable character outlines, so letters stay smooth at any size. Its data is arranged in individually tagged tables, which can hold glyph mappings, outlines, metrics and naming information. The registered media type is font/ttf.

The naming table is how a program learns a font's name, and it is where a specimen takes its heading from. A font file with a broken table or a bad offset can fail to display at all.

### Programs that open TTF files

**Windows, Mac and Linux**

- FontForge: opens TrueType outlines for editing, including the tables.

**Windows**

- Windows Font Previewer: double-click the font to inspect it before installing.

**Mac**

- Font Book: installs and validates font files.

**Linux**

- GNOME Fonts: previews installed typefaces and installs downloaded .ttf files.

### TTF and PNG compared

- **What they store**: a TTF stores outlines, character mappings and metrics. A PNG stores a grid of pixels, losslessly compressed, with optional transparency.
- **Scaling**: a font scales to any size. A PNG stays at the pixel size it was drawn.
- **Text**: a font can set any words you type. A PNG shows only what was drawn into it, and it cannot be installed.
- **Use**: a TTF goes into an operating system or an app. A PNG goes into a web page, a slide, a document or a review thread, so people can see a typeface without installing it.

Here is how the specimen is made. ImageMagick, compiled to WebAssembly, loads the font in your browser and draws with FreeType. The top line is the font's name, taken from its name table (the full name, or the family name if there is no full name), cut to 64 characters, and a font with no usable name is labeled "TTF font". Below it come the capital letters, the small letters, and the digits with a few punctuation marks. Five more lines repeat one familiar test sentence, each at its own size of 16, 24, 32, 48 and 64 pixels. Everything is black on white inside a 40 pixel margin. The image is only as wide as the longest line needs, between 400 and 2400 pixels. You cannot change the text. It is a specimen, not the font's outlines and not a character map. The download is named after your file with a .png ending, and the TTF itself is not changed.

### Other ways to convert TTF to PNG

- **ImageMagick:** run `magick display-face.ttf display-face-preview.png`. ImageMagick's TTF reader gives a preview image of the font.
- **Pillow (Python):** load the font with `ImageFont.truetype`, which loads a TrueType or OpenType font file at the pixel size you give. If the file is not at the given path, Pillow may search the standard font directories for your operating system, and it raises an OSError when the file cannot be read. Create a canvas with `Image.new`, draw your sample with `ImageDraw.text` and that font, then call `save` with a .png name. This takes a short script, but you choose the phrase, colors and size.
- **GIMP:** with the font available in the font selector, create an image, choose the Text tool, pick the font and size, type your sample and export with File > Export As, choosing PNG. The PNG holds pixels, not an editable text layer.

### Problems with TTF files

- **A font that never shows up**: a damaged font can fail to display. Font Book on a Mac can validate a font file.
- **Two copies conflict**: installing two copies of a font can create conflicts, and Font Book can resolve duplicates.
- **It is missing in an app**: a font missing from a third-party application may require that application's own troubleshooting.
- **The converter says it isn't a font**: FreeType could not read the file. Check that it opens in a font previewer.
- **The converter says it has no letters to draw**: the font has no glyphs for the sample lines, as can happen with an icon or symbol font. Draw your own sample with Pillow or GIMP.
- **You need the glyph outlines**: a PNG cannot give them. Open the TTF in FontForge.

guide.title: About TXT files
guide.markdown:
### What is a TXT file?

Nothing but characters are held in a TXT file. There are no typographic commands in it, and it dictates no page layout, typeface or placement of pictures, so any editor on any operating system can read it. Its MIME label is text/plain, and the charset parameter tells a receiver how the bytes map to characters.

A styled document turns into plain text when it is saved as TXT, since TextEdit strips the styles and formatting when it converts rich text. What the characters look like is decided by whoever opens the file, not by the file.

### Programs that open TXT files

**Windows, Mac and Linux**

- Visual Studio Code: a code editor that opens text files and lets you edit them.
- Vim: a text editor with Windows builds and documented Unix and macOS use.

**Mac**

- TextEdit: the Mac editor that works with plain text documents.

### TXT and JPG compared

- **What they store**: a TXT stores characters and line breaks. A JPG stores a grid of pixels, compressed with some loss, with an adjustable quality setting and no alpha transparency.
- **Look**: a TXT has no typeface of its own. A JPG fixes one, because the letters are already drawn into the picture.
- **Editing**: text in a TXT can be searched, copied and edited. Text in a JPG cannot be selected.
- **Support**: a TXT opens in any text editor, and a JPG is supported everywhere, so the picture is the safer choice when a destination takes only images.
- **Origin**: the Joint Photographic Experts Group defined JPG (ISO/IEC 10918-1) for photographs. The endings .jpg and .jpeg mean the same format.

Here is what the page does with your file. It decodes the bytes, drops terminal color codes and control characters, and turns each tab into spaces at stops every four characters. The text is then drawn on a canvas in your browser as dark text on white in DejaVu Sans. Lines that run long are folded at word breaks, and a single word wider than the page is cut. The picture is drawn at twice its size whenever it stays within 4,096 pixels a side, and the finished canvas is saved as a JPG at 0.85 quality. A text longer than one picture holds is cut, the last line of the picture says where, and the page shows the same notice. Your original TXT is not changed.

### Other ways to convert TXT to JPG

- **GIMP:** create an image and choose the Text tool. Turn on the editor window ("Use editor window") and load the TXT file with the folder icon in the text editor. Pick the font and size, drag a frame so the text fits, then use File > Export As and choose JPEG. GIMP puts the text on a new layer, and the size control offers several units. Check that no text runs off the canvas.
- **ImageMagick:** run `magick -background white -fill black -pointsize 24 -size 800x caption:@notes.txt notes-card.jpg`. The caption: operator word-wraps long lines to the width you give with -size, and -font picks a typeface. The -pointsize option really controls the spacing between lines, newlines in the file act as paragraph separators, and -size is required so the wrapping has a width. A security policy can block reading text from a file.
- **Pillow (Python):** read the TXT with the right encoding, create a canvas with `Image.new` (its default color is black, so pass white), draw the lines with `ImageDraw.multiline_text` and a font, and call `save` with a .jpg name. Text containing newlines passed to `ImageDraw.text` is handed to `multiline_text`, and drawing changes the image in place. You decide the size, wrapping and page breaks.

### Problems with TXT files

- **Accented letters look odd**: a file read with the wrong encoding shows valid characters as the wrong ones. Re-save it as UTF-8.
- **Formatting disappeared**: a styled document saved as TXT loses its styling.
- **A table or image is missing**: plain text cannot preserve an image or table as a word processor would.
- **The text is very long**: a picture ends at 4,096 pixels, so a long log or manuscript is cut. Split the text into smaller files.
- **The converter reports an empty file**: a file with nothing but spaces and control characters leaves nothing to draw. Open it in an editor and check that the text is really there.

guide.title: Understanding TXT and PNG
guide.markdown:
### What is a TXT file?

Nothing but plain text sits inside a TXT file: characters without fonts, styles or pictures, which is why every text editor on every operating system can read one. Its MIME label is text/plain. Plain text holds no typographic formatting commands and sets no page layout, font or placement of embedded images.

TXT is commonly used for notes and logs, configuration and readme files, and for exchanging text between programs. The bytes in a TXT file stand for characters through a character encoding, such as UTF-8, and the charset parameter tells a receiver which one. TextEdit on a Mac can convert rich text to TXT, and doing so removes the styles and formatting. A TXT file also can't keep an image or a table the way a word processor would.

### Programs that open TXT files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** Visual Studio Code edits text files in its file-based editor, and Vim is another editor for plain text.
- **Windows:** Notepad is listed as able to open TXT.
- **Mac:** TextEdit opens, edits and saves plain text documents.
- **Web:** any web browser can open a text file.

### TXT and PNG compared

- **Extensions and types**: .txt with text/plain, and .png with image/png.
- **What each is**: a TXT file is characters. A PNG is a picture, so the words become pixels and can no longer be searched, selected or edited.
- **Compression**: PNG compression never loses data and uses DEFLATE.
- **Color**: a PNG can be indexed, grayscale or truecolor, with 1 to 16 bits per sample, plus an optional alpha channel for transparency.
- **History**: The aim behind PNG was a replacement for GIF free of patents. October 1996 saw it become the first format issued as a W3C Recommendation; ISO/IEC 15948 followed.
- **Structure**: a PNG file starts with a fixed signature and is then built from chunks, such as IHDR for the header, IDAT for image data and IEND to close the file.
- **Standard**: W3C made the third edition of the PNG specification a Recommendation on 24 June 2025.
- **Support**: every major browser displays PNG, and macOS saves screenshots as PNG files by default.

Your text is drawn in your browser, on a canvas. Letters are very dark gray on a white ground, set in DejaVu Sans: 16 pixels tall text, 24 pixels from one baseline to the next, and a 32 pixel margin around the block. A line breaks between words at 800 pixels, roughly 90 characters, and a word too long for one line is broken inside. Tabs stop every 4 characters. Control characters, terminal color codes among them, are stripped. The image is as wide as its longest line, and it is drawn at double size, which keeps zoomed-in text crisp, or smaller when the text is taller than 2048 pixels. A page holds at most 168 lines. Anything longer gets truncated; the image's final line says at which line it stopped, and the page displays a notice too.

DejaVu Sans covers Latin, Greek, Cyrillic, Hebrew and Arabic. Other scripts fall back to your browser's own sans-serif font. The file is read as UTF-8, or UTF-16 when a byte order mark says so, and anything else is read as Windows-1252. Only the lines shown are measured, so a very long file is still drawn quickly. Select several TXT files and each is drawn into a PNG of its own, with your originals unchanged.

### Other ways to convert TXT to PNG

- **ImageMagick:** run `magick text:notes.txt notes.png`. ImageMagick's text pages use a letter-size canvas of 612x792 pixels by default and don't wrap long lines, and too many lines give several pages and so several images.

### Problems with TXT files

- **Different systems, different looks**: plain text does not prescribe a page layout or a font, so the same TXT file can look different from one editor to the next.
- **Wrong characters**: choosing the wrong character encoding makes characters appear as others. Save the file as UTF-8 before converting.
- **Styling is gone**: saving a styled document as TXT discards its formatting, so the PNG has none either.
- **A table or picture is missing**: a text file holds no images or tables as a word processor document would.
- **Nothing to draw**: an empty file is refused with "This text file is empty: there's no text to draw."

faqs.question: How do I make a GIF from just part of a video?

faqs.question: Which video formats can I use here?

faqs.answer: No. The page works with video files on your device and has no box for links. Use a clip you recorded or have the right to use.

faqs.question: Is the GIF high quality?
faqs.answer: It is made for short, small clips: 480 px on the longer side, 15 frames a second and 256 colors per frame. Fine text, fast motion and soft gradients lose the most.

faqs.question: Can I change the GIF's size, speed or frame rate?

faqs.question: How long can the video be?
faqs.answer: There is no limit, but every second adds 15 images to the GIF. A few seconds make a handy file; a minute makes one that is slow to convert and heavy to share.

faqs.question: Does the GIF play on repeat?
faqs.answer: Yes. It is written to play over and over without stopping, which is how GIFs are usually shown in chats and on web pages.

faqs.question: What happens to the sound?
faqs.answer: It is dropped. GIF stores pictures only, so the result is silent.

guide.title: About video to GIF
guide.markdown:
### What is a video file?

A video file is a container with tracks inside. The container, such as MP4, MOV, WebM or AVI, decides how the tracks are packed and labeled. The codecs inside decide how the picture and sound are squeezed: H.264, HEVC, VP9 or AV1 for the picture, and AAC, MP3 or Opus for the sound. That is why two .mp4 files can play differently on the same device.

The picture track is a run of still frames, usually 24, 30 or 60 a second. Video codecs save space by storing most frames as changes from the ones before, so a long clip can still be small. A GIF has no such trick. Each frame is a separate picture, so turning video into GIF is really choosing which stills to keep and how to color them.

This page takes MP4, the most common video format, from phones, cameras, screen recorders and editors. Other containers have their own pages: [MOV to GIF](/mov-to-gif/), [WebM to GIF](/webm-to-gif/) and [AVI to GIF](/avi-to-gif/).

### Programs that play and trim video files

**Windows**

- Media Player: the built-in player for MP4 and most common video.
- Microsoft Clipchamp: trims clips and can export short ones as GIF.
- VLC: plays nearly any video, with its own codecs.

**Mac**

- QuickTime Player: plays MP4 and MOV, and Edit > Trim cuts a clip down.
- iMovie: Apple's free editor for longer edits.

**Linux**

- VLC and mpv: free players.
- FFmpeg: cuts, scales and converts from the terminal.

**Web**

- Browsers: MP4 with H.264 plays in all the major ones.

**Mobile**

- iPhone and iPad: the Photos app trims a video in its editor.
- Android: Google Photos and most gallery apps can trim a clip before you share it.

### Video and GIF compared

- **Frames**: video often runs at 30 or 60 frames a second. This page keeps 15, so a 4-second clip becomes 60 images in the GIF.
- **Size of the picture**: the GIF is at most 480 px on its longer side, with both sides rounded down to an even number. A 1920x1080 clip comes out at 480x270.
- **Color**: a video frame can use millions of colors. A GIF image uses a palette of at most 256, so this page reads the whole clip first, builds one palette that suits it, then maps every frame onto that palette.
- **Compression**: video stores differences between frames. GIF stores each frame with LZW, which is lossless, but it can't predict motion, so a GIF is usually much larger than a video of the same length and size.
- **Sound**: video can carry it; GIF can't.
- **Playback**: a GIF starts by itself and needs no player, which is why chat apps, forums and email accept it where they block video. The GIF made here loops forever.
- **Media types**: video/mp4 for MP4; image/gif for GIF, a format CompuServe introduced in 1987.

### Other ways to convert video to GIF

- **Adobe Photoshop (Windows, Mac)**: import the clip with File > Import > Video Frames to Layers, turn the layers into a frame animation in Window > Timeline, then export with File > Export > Save for Web (Legacy) and choose GIF. Photoshop reads MP4, MOV, AVI and MPEG when the right codecs are installed, and may not import a long video in full.
- **Microsoft Clipchamp (Windows, web)**: put the clip on a project timeline, press Export in the top-right corner and pick GIF. Clipchamp offers GIF only for videos up to 15 seconds long.
- **FFmpeg (command line)**: `ffmpeg -i input.mp4 output.gif` works, but its palette is a general-purpose one that isn't tuned to the clip. For truer color, make a palette from the clip first with the palettegen filter and apply it with paletteuse, the method this page uses. Frame timing in a GIF counts in hundredths of a second, so no delay can be shorter than 0.01 s.

### Problems with video to GIF

- **The page won't take your file**: it accepts MP4 only. Use the converter for your video's format.
- **The GIF is too heavy to post**: shorten the clip before converting. Every second adds 15 frames, so the file grows with the length.
- **Small text is unreadable**: the 480 px limit shrinks screen recordings a lot. Crop to the part that matters, or share the video instead.
- **Shading turns into dots or steps**: 256 colors per frame can't hold a smooth gradient. Clips with flat colors convert best.
- **It takes a long time**: FFmpeg runs on your device in a single thread. Keep the tab open, and on a laptop plug in.
- **"FFmpeg failed with exit code N"**: the video couldn't be read. Make sure it plays in your usual player; if it doesn't, the file is probably damaged or incomplete.
- **You wanted the audio**: a GIF has none. The [MP4 to MP3 converter](/mp4-to-mp3/) saves the sound instead.

infoArticle.title: About video transcription

Video to Transcript transcribes speech from audio or video files. Uploaded files are processed in your browser. If you paste a direct link to an audio or video file, the server fetches the file and streams it to your browser for transcription. YouTube, TikTok, SoundCloud, and other webpage links are not supported right now. The speech model downloads on first use and runs locally.

This tool is best for interviews, meetings, lectures, and voice notes. Larger files take longer to process and may use more memory.

- Handles uploads or direct links to audio and video files.
- Creates a plain text transcript you can edit or share.
- Works with common audio and video formats.

faqs.question: Do my files get uploaded?

faqs.answer: The speech model downloads the first time you run the tool. After that it is cached for faster use.

tool.title: WAV to AAC
tool.subtitle: Encode a WAV recording as a 192 kbps AAC stream you can send and play.

seo.title: Convert WAV to AAC Online (Free)
seo.description: Convert WAV to AAC in your browser. FFmpeg encodes AAC-LC at 192 kbps into a standalone .aac stream. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.question: How do I convert WAV to AAC?
faqs.answer: Add the WAV above and FFmpeg encodes it locally in the browser, ready to download as AAC. If you add more files, each one is encoded in turn.

faqs.question: What is the AAC's bitrate?
faqs.answer: 192 kbps, fixed by the converter. The page has no bitrate setting. For another rate, use the FFmpeg command listed further down.

faqs.question: Does the page trim the audio or change its volume?
faqs.answer: No. The command has no trim, volume or fade option, so the AAC covers the whole WAV. Any video in the file is ignored.

faqs.question: Is the AAC the same as M4A?
faqs.answer: No. This page writes a standalone .aac file, a raw AAC stream in ADTS frames. M4A wraps AAC in an MP4 container, and renaming .aac to .m4a does not change the framing. Use WAV to M4A if an app wants the MP4 wrapper.

faqs.question: Does the AAC lose quality?
faqs.answer: Yes. AAC is lossy, so it discards detail the ear is least likely to miss. Keep the WAV in case you want to edit or encode again.

faqs.question: Can I pick the sample rate or channels?
faqs.answer: Not on this page, because the command sets neither. The FFmpeg command listed further down takes a rate or channel option when you need one.

faqs.question: What kind of AAC is it?
faqs.answer: AAC-LC, the low complexity profile, made by FFmpeg's built-in AAC encoder. It does not make HE-AAC.

faqs.question: Which players open an .aac file?
faqs.answer: VLC can read a raw AAC stream, and FFmpeg decodes AAC as well. Renaming .aac to .m4a does not add an MP4 wrapper, so use WAV to M4A for an app that wants one.

faqs.question: What does the "FFmpeg failed" error mean?
faqs.answer: FFmpeg could not encode that file. Try opening the WAV in Audacity or VLC first. Some recorders put proprietary compression inside WAV, and Audacity suggests its FFmpeg library for those files.

faqs.question: Does my WAV leave my device?
faqs.answer: No. The encoding happens through FFmpeg compiled to WebAssembly, running in a worker of your own browser, so no server sees the audio. The WAV is not modified; the AAC is a separate download.

toFormat.name: AAC

points: The AAC is 192 kbps AAC-LC in a standalone ADTS stream. You cannot change the bitrate on the page.
No sample rate, channel count, trim or volume change is set by the command.
The conversion is lossy. Keep the WAV as the master.

Each WAV gives its own AAC.

guide.title: About WAV files
guide.markdown:
### What is a WAV file?

Sound stored in a WAV file sits inside a RIFF wrapper, so WAV names a container, not a single way of encoding audio. The August 1991 multimedia specification from Microsoft and IBM described it. Most WAV files contain linear PCM, the plain sampled form, but other encodings can ride in the same wrapper, which means two .wav files can differ a great deal inside. You will see audio/wav and audio/x-wav used as media types.

PCM is uncompressed, which makes WAV files big but exact. Broadcast WAVE is the variant that holds metadata used in production and in preservation, and the Library of Congress names WAVE among the formats it recommends for audio collections. Keeping a WAV master and making an AAC for listening is a common split. The usual filename ending is .wav.

### Programs that open WAV files

**Windows, Mac and Linux**

- Audacity: opens most WAV recordings, including PCM variants.
- ffplay: the player bundled with FFmpeg, which includes a WAV demuxer and plays WAV files from the command line.

**Mobile**

- Firefox for Android: plays WAV, which Mozilla lists among its supported Android audio types.
- VLC for Android: a free media player for Android phones and tablets, whose decoding follows from the media inside the container.
- mpv for Android: an Android port linked by the mpv project.

### WAV and AAC compared

- **Encoding**: WAV is a wrapper that usually holds uncompressed linear PCM. AAC is a perceptual, lossy codec, standardized as MPEG-2 Part 7 and MPEG-4 Part 3.
- **Packaging**: AAC can be carried in MP4, QuickTime or other wrappers. A freestanding .aac file normally uses ADTS framing and is labeled audio/aac.
- **Profiles**: AAC comes as LC, HE-AAC and HE-AAC v2.
- **Quality**: linear PCM in a WAV is lossless. AAC discards detail in exchange for a compressed stream, and was standardized as the successor to MP3.
- **Use**: WAV suits recording and editing masters. AAC is used for streaming audio and end-user delivery.

On this page, FFmpeg runs inside your browser as WebAssembly and nothing is uploaded. It ignores any video, encodes the audio with its own AAC encoder at 192 kbps and writes an ADTS stream. No sample rate, channel count, trim or volume change is set by the command. A batch of WAV files is processed one by one, and each result is a separate .aac named after its WAV. Your original WAV stays unchanged. The codec is lossy, so converting the AAC back to WAV later will not restore the audio: encode from the original WAV, and avoid editing and re-encoding the AAC again and again.

The AAC comes out as a freestanding ADTS stream. FFmpeg's ADTS muxer accepts a single AAC stream, which is why the audio is written alone, and an app that wants an MP4 wrapper should be given the M4A converter's output instead.

### Other ways to convert WAV to AAC

- **FFmpeg:** `ffmpeg -i session.wav -vn -c:a aac -b:a 192k session-listen.aac` on the command line. Here -vn drops video, -c:a aac selects FFmpeg's own AAC encoder and -b:a fixes the bitrate. Add a sample rate or channel option when a delivery spec calls for one.
- **Audacity with FFmpeg:** load the WAV, open File > Export Audio and pick Custom FFmpeg Export. In the format options choose a format and an AAC codec, which depends on how FFmpeg was built. This needs Audacity's optional FFmpeg library.
- **WavePad:** open the WAV and choose File > Save As, then pick AAC. NCH lists AAC writing for Windows and Mac. Because AAC is lossy, avoid repeated editing generations of the same file.

### Problems with WAV files

- **Import fails**: some recorders put proprietary compression into the WAV, a case where Audacity suggests installing its FFmpeg library.
- **A very large recording**: the original RIFF size fields top out near 4 GB, so recordings past them may need RF64, and a program built for the old layout may not handle such a file.
- **Tags are missing or odd**: tags kept in INFO chunks and in Broadcast WAVE extensions differ, so programs treat metadata differently.
- **One WAV opens and another does not**: WAV can wrap PCM or compressed audio, so programs differ in what they accept.

guide.title: Understanding WAV and AIFF
guide.markdown:
### What is a WAV file?

WAV (also written WAVE) stands for Waveform Audio File Format. Microsoft and IBM built it on the RIFF container and described it in a multimedia specification published in August 1991. The file wraps sound but does not fix one encoding, and linear PCM is the usual contents, which makes a WAV big and exact, though compressed audio can sit inside as well.

A program therefore needs a decoder that matches whatever the WAV holds. Files end in .wav, and audio/wav and audio/x-wav are the media types you will see. A Broadcast WAVE variant carries production and archiving metadata, and the US Library of Congress names WAVE as its recommended format for digital sound collections. The size fields in the original design limit a file to 4 GB; longer recordings may use RF64.

### Programs that open WAV files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** Audacity imports most WAV recordings, including PCM variants, and ffplay, which ships with FFmpeg, plays a WAV through FFmpeg's WAV demuxer.
- **Web:** Firefox plays supported media itself, and Mozilla's list of audio types for Firefox on Android includes WAV.
- **Mobile:** The free VLC app on Android decodes according to what the file contains, while mpv on Android, a port linked by the mpv project, plays it too.

### WAV and AIFF compared

- **Extensions and types**: .wav with audio/wav, and .aiff or .aif with audio/aiff or audio/x-aiff.
- **Origins**: WAV came from Microsoft and IBM in 1991. Apple developed AIFF in 1988.
- **Container**: AIFF is derived from Electronic Arts' IFF family. WAV is derived from RIFF.
- **Sound**: both usually carry uncompressed linear PCM. AIFF-C extends the family to compressed audio.
- **Metadata**: AIFF can include named chunks for author, copyright and annotations.
- **Use**: professional audio users use AIFF for masters and intermediate recordings.
- **Opening the AIFF**: Audacity can import most AIFF files, and every PCM variant, without its optional FFmpeg library. Adobe Audition will open uncompressed AIFF too, along with the common compressed variants.
- **Specification**: Apple dated version 1.3 of the AIFF specification January 4, 1989.
- **Size**: WAV and AIFF files are limited to 4 GB, a general restriction and not an Audacity one. Many players are said to manage only files up to 2 GB.
- **CDs**: Audacity's manual says AIFF is suitable for burning an exported file to an audio CD.

Your WAV goes through FFmpeg in your browser, which writes the sound as 16-bit PCM in an AIFF file with the bytes in big-endian order. That is plain, uncompressed audio like the WAV's, so a 16-bit WAV keeps its samples. A WAV that holds 24-bit or floating-point audio is written at 16 bits. Only audio is written, since the command leaves out any video stream, and your original WAV is left as it was; the AIFF is a new file you download. Choose several WAVs and they convert one after another. If the conversion fails, the message names FFmpeg and gives its exit code.

### Other ways to convert WAV to AIFF

- **FFmpeg from a terminal:** run `ffmpeg -i session.wav -c:a pcm_s16be listening.aiff`.
- **Audacity:** load the WAV, open the Export Audio dialog, select the AIFF 16-bit PCM format (it has no options) and save. AIFF files are capped at 4 GB, a limit of the format itself.

### Problems with WAV files

- **It won't open**: the WAV may carry a proprietary compression from the recorder. Audacity recommends its FFmpeg library for importing such files.
- **A player opens one WAV and not another**: linear PCM or compressed audio can sit inside a WAV, so a program that plays one WAV can still refuse another.
- **The file is huge**: raw PCM needs more room than a delivery copy of the recording in compressed form.
- **A recording over 4 GB**: the original RIFF size fields can't describe it, and very large recordings may require RF64.
- **Tags look different afterward**: the INFO chunks of a WAV and the Broadcast WAVE extensions store different information, so programs treat metadata in different ways.
- **An author field looks misplaced**: Adobe Audition may show an AIFF author field as Dublin Core: Creator rather than as Author.
- **An AIFF-C won't play**: it needs a decoder for its particular encoding; knowing the family name does not guarantee support.

guide.title: About WAV files
guide.markdown:
### What is a WAV file?

WAVE audio files, written .wav, use the RIFF chunk structure. Microsoft and IBM published the layout in a 1991 multimedia specification, and it describes a wrapper rather than a fixed encoding. Linear PCM is what you will usually find inside. Compressed audio is allowed too, so the extension alone cannot tell you what a given file holds. Common media types are audio/wav and audio/x-wav.

A variant called Broadcast WAVE carries extra metadata for production and preservation. The Library of Congress recommends the format for audio collections. As a source for a ringtone, a WAV is a good place to start because it usually holds uncompressed PCM, which makes files big but exact. The format record puts the original size limit at 4 GB.

### Programs that open WAV files

**Windows, Linux and Mac**

- ffplay: the player that ships with FFmpeg has a WAV demuxer, so it can play the WAV from the command line before you convert it.
- Audacity: reads the common WAV recordings, PCM variants included.

**Mobile**

- Android edition of VLC: plays media on phones and tablets, with decoding that depends on what the container holds.
- Firefox for Android: Mozilla lists WAV among the audio it plays directly.
- mpv for Android: a port the mpv project links to, which plays the WAV on a phone or tablet.

### WAV and M4R compared

- **Encoding**: WAV usually holds uncompressed linear PCM. M4R holds compressed audio, typically AAC.
- **Container**: an MPEG-4 file keeps its wrapper structure apart from whatever encoding the tracks use. MediaInfo classifies .m4r within its MPEG-4 container family, and these files can carry track metadata besides the samples.
- **Purpose**: WAV is a recording master, while NCH's WavePad manual calls M4R the iPhone's ringtone type.
- **Length**: Apple's GarageBand ringtone workflow limits the selected sound to 30 seconds, so a longer WAV has to be shortened elsewhere, because this page does not trim.
- **Support**: WavePad lists .m4r opening and saving on Windows, but not on Mac.

The conversion runs in your browser, where FFmpeg (WebAssembly) skips any video and converts the audio to AAC at 192 kbps. It writes the result with FFmpeg's iPod format, so the file is MPEG-4 audio that carries the .m4r name. The command leaves sample rate, channel count and length alone, so the ringtone runs as long as the WAV. The page does not install a ringtone either: you still have to add the M4R to the iPhone. Select a batch and every WAV is converted one at a time, each getting its own .m4r with the WAV's name. Your original WAV is not changed.

### Other ways to convert WAV to M4R

- **FFmpeg:** `ffmpeg -i cue.wav -t 30 -c:a aac -b:a 192k -vn -f ipod cue-tone.m4r` on the command line. In this command -vn drops video, -c:a and -b:a choose the AAC encoder and its bitrate, and -f ipod writes the MPEG-4 container. This example cuts the audio at 30 seconds with `-t 30`. It makes the file and does not assign a ringtone.
- **WavePad on Windows:** open the WAV, then choose File > Save As and pick M4R. NCH lists M4R saving for Windows only.
- **GarageBand on iPhone:** create a recording project, then use Tracks > Loops Browser > Files > Browse items from Files to bring the WAV into Tracks and trim it. Back in My Songs, pick the project, then Share, Ringtone and Export. This builds and installs the ringtone on the phone, within the 30-second limit, and GarageBand offers to shorten a longer export. A dimmed song cannot be picked until it has been downloaded to the iPhone.

### Problems with WAV files

- **It will not import**: some recorders put proprietary compression inside a WAV. Audacity points to its FFmpeg library for those imports.
- **The file is too big for an old program**: recordings that outgrow the original RIFF size fields may be stored as RF64, which a program built for the older layout may not read.
- **A player balks at one file**: the same wrapper holds PCM or compressed audio, so one program can accept a file that another refuses.
- **Titles or tags are odd**: INFO chunks and Broadcast WAVE extensions carry different information, so metadata is handled unevenly.

guide.title: Understanding WebM to AVI
guide.markdown:
### What is a WebM file?

The WebM Project promotes WebM as an open media format for web delivery, built on the Matroska container. It carries VP8 or VP9 video next to Vorbis or Opus audio, and the project supplies its format technology royalty-free. Its media types are video/webm for video files and audio/webm for sound-only ones.

### Programs that open WebM files

- **Windows, Mac, Linux, Android and iOS:** VLC media player reads Matroska-family media. The Android app carries the desktop player's decoding, and the iOS app plays local media without conversion.
- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** FFplay plays WebM through FFmpeg's decoders.
- **Web:** Safari on macOS added WebM in version 14.1; it covers VP8 and VP9 video plus Vorbis audio.

### WebM and AVI compared

- **AVI**: Microsoft's RIFF-based container, dating from Windows 3.1 and a 1992 specification. Its video may be raw, lossless or lossy, so a .avi name reveals nothing about quality.
- **Video**: written by the FFmpeg `mpeg4` encoder and tagged xvid.
- **Audio**: MP3 at 96 kbps.
- **Frame size**: 1920 px is the ceiling for the longer side, and each side is trimmed to an even pixel count.
- **Frame rate**: 30 fps at most.
- **Interlacing**: frames marked as interlaced are deinterlaced.
- **Tags**: the command has no `-map` or `-map_metadata`, so FFmpeg's defaults choose the streams and copy global tags, for example title or artist, wherever the AVI has a field for them.
- **Privacy**: FFmpeg is compiled to WebAssembly and works in your browser, so the WebM is not uploaded. Several files run one after another, each downloading as its own AVI.

### Other ways to convert WebM to AVI

- **FFmpeg:** run `ffmpeg -i clip.webm clip.avi`. FFmpeg guesses the output format from the file extension.

### Problems with WebM files

- **Seeking is slow**: a missing cue index leaves the player with less direct location information.
- **It plays in one app only**: the streams inside, rather than the .webm name, determine playback, so a player such as VLC must support them.
- **An old Safari will not play it**: WebM playback arrived on macOS only with Safari 14.1, and only for VP8 or VP9 video with Vorbis sound.

faqs.question: Why do pictures I save from websites come out as WebP?

faqs.question: Will the JPG be bigger than the WebP?

guide.title: About WebP files
guide.markdown:
### What is a WebP file?

WebP is an image format made by Google, announced in 2010 and released as open source. Its lossy mode borrows the key-frame coding of VP8, a video codec that began at On2 Technologies and that Google released as open source in May 2010. A lossless mode with its own method followed, and both modes can carry transparency and animation. Inside, a WebP is a RIFF container, the same wrapper WAV audio uses. RFC 9649, published in November 2024, documents the format and registers its media type, image/webp.

You mostly meet WebP on the web. Sites serve it because it is compact: Google reports lossy WebP files about 30% smaller than JPEG on average. So a picture saved from a browser often lands as .webp, and then an older editor, a print shop or an upload form that wants JPG won't take it. Animated WebP turns up too: WhatsApp's animated stickers, for example, are WebP files.

### Programs that open WebP files

**Windows**

- Photos and File Explorer: show WebP once Microsoft's WebP Image Extension is installed.
- Adobe Photoshop: opens and saves WebP from version 23.2; older versions need Google's WebPShop plug-in.
- GIMP: free editor that reads and writes WebP from version 2.10.
- XnView MP: viewer and converter, free for private use, that reads and writes WebP.

**Mac**

- Photoshop and GIMP: the same versions as on Windows.

**Linux**

- GIMP: the usual desktop choice for opening and exporting WebP.
- ImageMagick: converts on the command line when built with the WebP delegate library.

**Web**

- Chrome 17+, Edge 18+, Firefox 65+ and Safari 14+ display lossy WebP. Safari needs macOS Big Sur or later.

**Mobile**

- Android: decodes WebP from 4.0, and lossless or transparent WebP from 4.2.1.
- iPhone and iPad: Safari shows WebP from iOS 14.

### WebP and JPG compared

- **Extensions and media types**: .webp and image/webp; .jpg or .jpeg and image/jpeg.
- **Compression**: lossy WebP codes the picture as a VP8 key frame, and lossless WebP uses LZ77, prefix codes and a color cache. Baseline JPEG is always lossy: 8x8 blocks, a discrete cosine transform, then Huffman coding.
- **Transparency**: WebP has an alpha channel in both modes. JPG has none.
- **Animation**: WebP can hold timed frames. A JPG is one still picture.
- **Color depth**: both store 8 bits per channel.
- **Largest image**: 16,383 pixels a side for WebP, 65,535 for JPEG.
- **Reach**: almost any program, camera, printer or photo kiosk reads JPEG. WebP needs a recent browser or one of the programs above.
- **Metadata**: both can carry an ICC profile, Exif and XMP.

What changes in this conversion is the move to a format without transparency or animation. The page decodes the WebP to pixels and writes a JPG at quality 0.85. See-through areas can't stay see-through, an animation gives its first frame, and the metadata stays behind in the WebP.

### Other ways to convert WebP to JPG

- **Adobe Photoshop (Windows, Mac)**: open the WebP, choose File > Export > Export As, pick JPG and click Export. Version 23.2 or later opens WebP itself; older ones need the WebPShop plug-in.
- **GIMP (Windows, Mac, Linux)**: open the file in GIMP 2.10 or later, choose File > Export As, type a name ending in .jpg and click Export.
- **ImageMagick (command line)**: run `magick input.webp output.jpg`. The build must include the WebP delegate library.

### Problems with WebP files

- **Double-clicking does nothing on Windows**: install the WebP Image Extension from the Microsoft Store, or drag the file into a browser window.
- **A site or form rejects it**: convert it to JPG here, or to PNG with the [WebP to PNG converter](/webp-to-png/) when transparency must survive.
- **A renamed file still fails**: changing .webp to .jpg leaves WebP data inside, and strict programs check the data. Convert the file instead.
- **Only one frame came out**: a JPG can't animate, so an animated WebP gives its first frame. Keep the WebP if you need the motion.
- **"Image decode failed."**: the browser couldn't read the file, usually because it is damaged. Download it again from where you found it.
- **The JPG looks soft or blotchy**: a lossy WebP has already lost some detail, and the JPG is compressed again on top. Start from the largest, least compressed copy the site offers.

faqs.question: How do I convert WMV to AVI?
faqs.answer: Select the WMV above, wait for the conversion to end and save the AVI that appears.

faqs.question: What is inside the AVI I get?
faqs.answer: MPEG-4 Part 2 video with the Xvid tag at a fixed quality value of 10 with no B-frames, and MP3 audio at 96 kbps. AVI is only the wrapper, so these two codecs are what a player has to support.

faqs.question: What is the difference between WMV and AVI?
faqs.answer: WMV is Windows Media video, usually stored in Microsoft's ASF container. AVI, a RIFF-based container from Microsoft, can carry many codecs. Changing the extension does not change what is inside, which is why the video is re-encoded.

faqs.question: Will the AVI look worse than the WMV?
faqs.answer: It can. Both formats are lossy, and the AVI is encoded from the already-compressed WMV picture. Converting does not add detail.

faqs.question: Is my video resized?
faqs.answer: Only if it is big. A frame bigger than 1920 pixels in either direction is scaled down, and a clip above 30 fps drops frames to reach it while keeping its running time. Width and height are adjusted to even numbers.

faqs.question: Does the converter deinterlace the video?
faqs.answer: When a frame is flagged interlaced, yes. The yadif filter skips everything else, so progressive video is untouched.

faqs.question: What happens to the WMV's sound?
faqs.answer: The audio is decoded, then encoded again as 96 kbps MP3 by LAME, which makes it a second lossy generation.

faqs.question: Can I rename a .wmv file to .avi?
faqs.answer: No, because the name is only a label and the bytes inside stay Windows Media. Any program that inspects the contents will reject it. Converting is what produces genuine AVI data.

faqs.question: Can I convert a batch of WMV files?
faqs.answer: Yes. Several WMVs give several AVIs, made one at a time and never joined into a single movie.

faqs.question: Is there a size limit for the WMV?
faqs.answer: The page sets none. The original AVI design had size restrictions that a later extension, OpenDML, lifted, so a very long recording may need a player that supports large AVI files.

guide.title: About WMV files
guide.markdown:
### What is a WMV file?

Windows Media content in the ASF container is what a WMV file holds. Microsoft designed ASF for synchronized media that can be stored on a disk or delivered over HTTP, and it carries audio and video streams. The video inside a WMV uses Windows Media Video compression, in version 7, 8 or 9, according to the Library of Congress. That entry also notes video/x-ms-wmv, a media type in common use that was never formally registered.

The ending names only the family, so two WMV files can use different compression versions. How good a WMV looks comes from the codec and settings used to make it, not from the extension.

ASF carries audio and video streams, and a file can be played from disk or fetched over HTTP. The video inside is Windows Media coded content, so the ASF wrapper and the compression are two separate things.

### Programs that open WMV files

**Windows, Linux and Mac**

- FFplay: the player that comes with FFmpeg, which decodes WMV with FFmpeg's own decoders.
- VLC media player: its feature list covers ASF and WMV input plus Windows Media Video decoders for versions 1, 2 and 9.

**Mobile**

- Android port of VLC: brings the desktop player's decoding to Android.
- iOS port of VLC: plays files on the device with VLC's own engine, not the system player.

### WMV and AVI compared

- **Extensions**: .wmv and .avi. Neither ending says which codec is inside.
- **Container**: WMV uses ASF, built for streaming and synchronized delivery. AVI, which Microsoft introduced in 1992, is built on RIFF. It interleaves timed pictures and sound, and its header records dimensions and frame rate.
- **Codecs**: a WMV carries Windows Media Video. An AVI can carry uncompressed, lossless or lossy video, identified by FOURCC codes. The AVI made here holds Xvid-tagged MPEG-4 video (Part 2).
- **Size limits**: the first AVI design restricted file size, and the later OpenDML extension relaxed that.
- **Streaming**: ASF was built for network delivery as well as disk storage, while AVI is an interleaved file of timed pictures and sound.
- **Metadata**: AVI implementations do not all handle aspect ratio and scan type the same way.

What happens to your file here: FFmpeg, running in the browser, reads the ASF container and passes any frames marked as interlaced through a deinterlacer. Video larger than 1920 pixels is reduced to fit, faster motion is limited to 30 frames per second, and widths and heights are adjusted to even values. The video is encoded with FFmpeg's MPEG-4 encoder at quality value 10 with no B-frames, and the sound goes through the LAME MP3 encoder at 96 kbps. Both codecs are lossy, so the AVI is a second generation of the picture and cannot be sharper than the WMV. The download is named after the WMV with an .avi ending, and the original is not changed. Select a batch and each WMV becomes its own AVI, converted one after another and never merged; no ZIP is produced.

### Other ways to convert WMV to AVI

- **FFmpeg:** on the command line, `ffmpeg -i legacy.wmv -c:v mpeg4 -c:a libmp3lame legacy.avi`. It reads the WMV with FFmpeg's decoder for it and writes the AVI with the two encoders named in the command. The command re-encodes both streams instead of copying them, and the -c:v and -c:a options pick the encoders. FFmpeg guesses the output container from the file extension, so the .avi name is what asks for an AVI.

### Problems with WMV files

- **Sound plays but the picture is missing**: unpacking the ASF wrapper is one job and decoding the video inside is another, and a player may manage only the first. The FFmpeg codec list itself marks its Windows Media Video 9 decoder as incomplete, so files can behave differently from program to program. Try VLC, which lists ASF and WMV input, to see whether the file opens at all.
- **Two WMV files look different**: the family covers versions 7, 8 and 9, so the picture depends on the compression and settings used to make each file. Compare the files themselves, not their extensions, when one looks worse than another.
- **A player gets the wrapper but not the video**: reading ASF does not mean every codec inside is installed.

guide.title: About WMV and GIF files
guide.markdown:
### What is a WMV file?

The .wmv ending means Windows Media content inside an ASF container. Microsoft built ASF to store synchronized media and deliver it over networks, and it can hold audio and video streams, played from a disk or streamed from an HTTP server. Three generations of Windows Media Video compression, 7, 8 and 9, are found in WMV files. The media type in common use is video/x-ms-wmv, which the Library of Congress notes is not an IANA registration.

How faithful the picture is depends on the codec and its compression settings, so the .wmv ending alone says nothing about quality.

### Programs that open WMV files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** VLC media player counts ASF/WMV among its inputs and covers Windows Media Video 1, 2 and 9 in its decoding. FFplay plays WMV input with FFmpeg decoders.
- **Mobile:** on a phone, VLC for Android carries the desktop player's media decoding features, and VLC for iOS runs local files in VLC's player, and the system player is not involved.

### WMV and GIF compared

- **Names and types**: .wmv is video/x-ms-wmv, and .gif is image/gif.
- **Content**: WMV holds audio and video streams in ASF. GIF holds a series of images with a delay for each, counted in hundredths of a second.
- **Colors**: no GIF image can exceed a 256-color palette, and its transparency sets a single palette color fully clear, with no in-between.
- **Compression**: GIF compresses images losslessly with LZW coding.
- **History**: GIF was created at CompuServe in 1987; a July 1990 revision, GIF89a, added extensions covering transparency, timing, comments and application-specific data.
- **Display**: every major browser displays GIF.
- **Licensing**: LZW fees from Unisys began in 1994; the US patent expired in 2003, and the European and Japanese patents in 2004.
- **Looping**: GIMP can export layers as an animated GIF that repeats forever, as this page's output does.

FFmpeg works in two passes inside your browser. Pass one deinterlaces marked frames, takes 15 frames a second, scales the picture into a 480-pixel box with even sides, and derives a palette from what it sees. Pass two repeats the filtering and paints the frames from that palette. The result is set to repeat forever, the sound is dropped, and the whole video is processed. At 15 frames a second a one-minute clip becomes 900 separate images, so long videos give very large GIFs, and each frame is limited to the palette, so gradients may show visible steps. Cutting the clip down in an editor first keeps the GIF small, because the page has no trim control.

### Other ways to convert WMV to GIF

- **Microsoft Clipchamp:** add the WMV to a project, click Export, and choose GIF from the options. Clipchamp offers GIF for videos of 15 seconds or less, and WMV is on its list of supported imports.
- **FFmpeg, short excerpt (Windows, Mac, Linux):** run `ffmpeg -t 4 -i training.wmv excerpt.gif`. Because `-t` comes before `-i`, only the first four seconds of the input are read.
- **FFmpeg, palette pipeline (Windows, Mac, Linux):** run `ffmpeg -i training.wmv -vf palettegen wmv-colors.png`, then `ffmpeg -i training.wmv -i wmv-colors.png -lavfi paletteuse wmv-animation.gif`. Keep any trim and scale settings the same in both passes.

Both FFmpeg commands let you limit the length, which this page cannot. The palette pipeline generates one palette for the whole video, then uses it to downsample the stream.

### Problems with WMV files

- **Sound or text but no picture**: reading an ASF container and decoding the video inside it are different jobs, so a reader that opens the file may still lack the codec for the video.
- **Some WMV9 files misbehave**: FFmpeg's documentation says its Windows Media Video 9 support is not completely working. Try VLC to check that the file plays at all.
- **Quality varies from file to file**: fidelity follows the codec and compression settings the file was made with, not its ending.
- **The container and the codec differ**: a .wmv file uses ASF with Windows Media coded content, in Windows Media Video 7, 8 or 9 compression, so knowing the ending does not tell you which one a file holds.
- **Interlaced footage combs in the GIF**: only frames marked as interlaced are deinterlaced here, so unmarked interlaced footage keeps its combing.

guide.title: About XCF files
guide.markdown:
### What is an XCF file?

XCF is GIMP's native working-image format. The file keeps layers and transparency, so work can be resumed later and not just viewed as one flat picture. It also keeps channels, paths and selections, and GIMP uses it to retain editing information between sessions. Undo history is left out. GIMP's Save command writes XCF, while other image formats go through Export.

GIMP does not present XCF as a format for exchanging images. It is a project file meant for your own editing, so most ordinary image viewers cannot read it. That is the usual reason to turn it into something shareable.

### Programs that open XCF files

**Windows, Mac and Linux**

- GIMP: the native editor, and saving as XCF keeps the whole working image.
- ImageMagick: reads XCF, though an outside renderer may not reproduce every GIMP feature.

XCF is used for layered image editing and for saving work in progress, and it is lossless, so reopening the file in GIMP loses nothing.

### XCF and PDF compared

- **Purpose**: XCF is a working file for editing in GIMP. PDF is a fixed-page document made to be shared and read.
- **Layers**: XCF keeps layers and transparency. A PDF made here holds one picture on one page.
- **Page**: an XCF is a canvas of pixels. A PDF has a page size, so a viewer knows how large the page is.
- **Support**: few ordinary viewers read XCF, while PDF is readable in browsers and PDF readers.
- **Editing**: GIMP can reopen an XCF with every layer. A PDF of the picture cannot give the layers back.

Here is what the converter does. ImageMagick, compiled to WebAssembly, reads the XCF in your browser as a single picture, so layers are not turned into separate pages. The picture is then embedded in a PDF with pdf-lib. The document is one page sized to the picture, with each pixel counted as one point, so a canvas 1200 pixels wide makes a page 1200 points wide, about 16.7 inches. That leaves out margins and standard paper sizes. Inside ImageMagick the pixels are first turned into a PNG, and pdf-lib then places that PNG on the page. The picture goes in losslessly, which means the quality setting does not apply. Above about 537 megapixels the page declines the file with a note that it is too large. Several files are never combined into one PDF, and the XCF you chose is left unchanged. The download is named after the XCF with a .pdf ending.

### Other ways to convert XCF to PDF

- **GIMP:** open the XCF and choose File > Export As, or press Shift+Ctrl+E, which stores the image in a format other than XCF. Export it as PDF. The PDF options include Layers as pages, Reverse order, Root layers only, Apply layer masks, Omit hidden layers and Fill transparent areas with background color, which help for a page per layer or a solid backdrop. The dialog also offers Convert bitmaps to vector and Convert text layers to image, so check each option against what you want the PDF to hold.
- **ImageMagick:** run `magick project.xcf project-review.pdf`. ImageMagick's formats page lists XCF as read-only and says PDF output needs Ghostscript installed. Compare the result with what you see in GIMP, since ImageMagick is a different renderer from GIMP.
- **GIMP and Preview on a Mac:** export the picture you want from GIMP as a PNG and open it in Preview. Then choose File > Export, open the Format pop-up menu, choose PDF and save. Preview is working from the PNG here, not the XCF.

### Problems with XCF files

- **Other software can't read it**: common image viewers do not understand XCF, so export a copy from GIMP for viewing.
- **The export is flat**: a flattened export does not keep every project property. Keep the XCF for future editing.
- **GIMP asks to save on exit**: exporting leaves the XCF project unsaved, so the prompt still appears.
- **A layered file gives one picture**: this page reads the XCF as a single image, so a layer cannot be chosen here, and layers do not become pages. GIMP's own export has Layers as pages for that.
- **It appears different elsewhere**: outside programs do not replicate all of GIMP's features. Export from GIMP itself and check the output.

guide.title: About XLS and JPG
guide.markdown:
### What is an XLS file?

XLS is the binary workbook format of Microsoft Excel. The Excel 97-2003 version uses BIFF8, and Excel 5.0/95 used a BIFF5 variant with the same ending. A sheet holds up to 65,536 rows and 256 columns, and current Excel versions show such a file with the Compatibility Mode label. Its media type is application/vnd.ms-excel.

A workbook describes cells, not a picture. Before a JPG exists, you have to decide which cells it should show, since a sheet can run far past one screen. That is why the converter above can't do it alone: it reads image files, and XLS is not one. For a picture of every visible sheet, save the workbook as .xlsx and use the XLSX to JPG converter.

### Programs that open XLS files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** LibreOffice Calc reads Excel workbooks, including the legacy binary kind.
- **Windows:** Microsoft Excel loads a legacy workbook when you use File > Open.
- **Linux:** Gnumeric documents Excel import support.
- **Web:** Google Sheets imports Excel files. Excel for the web turns a legacy XLS into an XLSX working copy.
- **Mobile:** Numbers for iPhone imports .xls files, and Excel for Android and iOS opens a legacy XLS read-only.

### XLS and JPG compared

- **Contents**: XLS stores cells, formulas, formatting and charts. JPG stores a grid of pixels and nothing else.
- **Compression**: JPG is lossy, so thin gridlines and small text can smear.
- **Editing**: the image can't be recalculated or sorted.
- **Layout**: the picture shows only the range you copy, so the columns and rows on screen decide what appears.

### Other ways to convert XLS to JPG

- **Excel and PowerPoint:** select the cells, pick Copy as Picture from the Copy drop-down of the Home tab. In the Copy Picture dialog set Appearance to As shown on screen and Format to Picture, then click OK. Paste into PowerPoint with Ctrl+V, right-click the pasted picture, choose Save as Picture and select JPEG as the file type. The result matches what the cells look like on screen.

### Problems with XLS files

- **Modern features go missing**: worksheet features can be lost when a workbook is saved as Excel 97-2003.
- **Cells beyond the limits**: an XLS cannot hold cells outside its older row and column limits.
- **Small text smears**: capture fewer cells per image instead of shrinking a large range.

guide.title: Understanding XLSX to JPG
guide.markdown:
### What is an XLSX file?

XLSX is Microsoft Excel's XML workbook format, used since Excel 2007. A workbook is a ZIP package of Open Packaging Conventions parts, and several of those parts are XML documents. XLSX cannot store VBA code or Excel 4.0 macro sheets. Its media type is application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet.

### Programs that open XLSX files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** LibreOffice Calc opens Excel workbook formats and imports Open XML Excel workbooks.
- **Windows and Mac:** Microsoft Excel opens the workbook through File > Open.
- **Mac:** Apple Numbers imports .xls and .xlsx files for editing.
- **Linux:** Gnumeric documents Office Open XML import.
- **Web:** Google Sheets imports Excel files, and Excel for the web opens XLSX directly.
- **Mobile:** Numbers for iPhone imports XLSX, and Microsoft Excel for Android and iOS can edit it.

### XLSX and JPG compared

- **Sheets**: each visible sheet with values becomes one image, in order.
- **Values**: cells show what Excel shows, and formulas show their saved results.
- **Left out**: hidden sheets, rows and columns, plus charts, pictures, comments and colors.
- **Size**: images stop at 4096 px a side, and a note appears when rows or columns do not fit.
- **Refused**: XLS files and password-protected workbooks.
- **Original**: your workbook is not changed and, since the page runs in your browser, not uploaded. You download new JPG files.
- **Formulas**: a JPG of a sheet is a picture of its table and keeps no formulas, so keep the XLSX for calculations.

### Other ways to convert XLSX to JPG

- **Excel and GIMP:** select a range and use Home > Copy > Copy as Picture. Paste into GIMP via Edit > Paste as > Paste as New Image, and finish with File > Export As, saving a JPEG.
- **LibreOffice Calc and GIMP:** choose File > Export As > Export as PDF, open the PDF in GIMP, where a dialog asks which page to import, and export a JPEG.
- **Numbers and Preview:** in Numbers, export through File > Export To > PDF. Then open the PDF in Preview and save it with File > Export, choosing JPEG as the format.

### Problems with XLSX files

- **Saved as a CSV, formatting disappears**: a CSV keeps only the active sheet's data.
- **A macro workbook loses its code**: saving as XLSX cannot retain VBA, so use a macro-enabled format.
- **Very large files**: the page reads sheets within set limits, and a sheet that goes over them is left out and named.

faqs.question: Can you convert XML to PDF?
faqs.answer: Yes, as a listing. The PDF shows your XML's content, one line a node, with each level of nesting indented two columns further, up to 20 levels. It is not the file styled by a stylesheet.

faqs.question: How do I convert XML to PDF?
faqs.answer: Choose one or more XML files above. Each is read in your browser and saved as a PDF named after the file, and each PDF downloads on its own.

faqs.question: What size are the PDF pages?
faqs.answer: A4 portrait with 3/4 inch margins, in 10 pt type: 61 lines a page and 81 characters a line in Courier. A longer line wraps. No header, footer or page numbers are added.

faqs.question: Why does it say my XML isn't well-formed?
faqs.answer: The file broke XML's rules, for example an unclosed tag, an unquoted attribute value or a second root element. The message gives what the parser found and the line and column where it stopped, so you can fix the file and convert it again.

faqs.question: What happens to entities and the DOCTYPE?
faqs.answer: XML's five built-in entities and character references are shown as the characters they stand for. Any other entity is shown as written, never expanded or fetched, so a file that refers to other files converts like any other and loads nothing.

faqs.question: Which characters can it show?
faqs.answer: Text that is all Windows-1252 characters is set in Courier. Anything else is set in DejaVu Sans, embedded in the PDF, which covers scripts such as Arabic and Hebrew. Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Indic and Thai characters and emoji are refused, with the characters named, rather than saved as blank boxes.

faqs.question: Can it turn an e-invoice or an XSL-FO file into a formatted document?
faqs.answer: No. It lists any XML file's content, but it doesn't apply an invoice's layout or an XSL-FO or XSLT stylesheet.

faqs.question: How large a file can I convert?
faqs.answer: Up to 20 MB, making up to 2,000 pages. A larger file is refused with a message saying which limit it passed.

faqs.question: Can mutool write JPEG directly?

faqs.question: Why does renaming the file to .jpg not work?

faqs.question: Will the text stay selectable in the JPG?

faqs.question: How sharp will the JPG be?

guide.title: About XPS and JPG
guide.markdown:
### What is an XPS file?

XPS stands for XML Paper Specification. It is a fixed-layout format for electronic documents and printing, built from XML inside Open Packaging Conventions. Every page keeps its layout instead of reflowing, the document is a list of fixed documents and fixed pages, and fonts can be embedded. Its registered media type is application/vnd.ms-xpsdocument.

The converter above reads image files, so it cannot render an XPS. Use a program that understands XPS to draw the pages, then save them as JPGs.

### Programs that open XPS files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:** the MuPDF viewer lists XPS among its supported formats.
- **Windows:** SumatraPDF is a free Windows reader with XPS support.
- **Mac:** `mutool draw` reads XPS pages for rendering.
- **Linux:** Okular lists XPS among its document handlers.

### XPS and JPG compared

- **Layout**: XPS describes pages with fixed positions. JPG is one picture, so a multi-page XPS becomes one JPG per page.
- **Text**: XPS keeps its text as text. In a JPG it is part of the pixels, so searching and copying stop working.
- **Fonts**: an XPS can embed its fonts, so the page looks the same on any machine. A JPG has no fonts to lose.
- **Compression**: JPG is lossy, so fine rules and small type need a high render resolution.

### Other ways to convert XPS to JPG

- **MuPDF and ImageMagick:** `mutool draw -r 150 -o page-%d.png document.xps` writes a PNG for every page at 150 dpi. Then run `magick page-1.png page-1.jpg` on each one you want. mutool cannot write JPEG itself, so the PNG step is needed.

### Problems with XPS files

- **Only one page came out**: use %d in the output name so every page gets a file.
- **The text looks fuzzy**: render again with a higher `-r` value.
- **A viewer won't open it**: use one that lists XPS support, such as SumatraPDF or MuPDF.
- **Annotations or forms are missing**: viewer features differ by format, so don't assume PDF annotations or forms also work in XPS.
- **You need to edit the pages**: an XPS page description is not the editable source, so keep the original authoring file.

infoArticle.title: About YouTube transcription
infoArticle.markdown:
YouTube to Transcript transcribes speech from audio or video files. Uploaded files are processed in your browser. If you paste a direct link to an audio or video file, the server fetches the file and streams it to your browser for transcription. YouTube, TikTok, SoundCloud, and other webpage links are not supported right now. The speech model downloads on first use and runs locally.

This tool is best for interviews, meetings, lectures, and voice notes. Larger files take longer to process and may use more memory.

**Why use this tool**

- Handles uploads or direct links to audio and video files.
- Creates a plain text transcript you can edit or share.
- Works with common audio and video formats.

faqs.question: Do my files get uploaded?
faqs.answer: Uploads are processed locally in your browser. If you paste a direct link to an audio or video file, the server fetches the file and streams it to your browser. The model files are downloaded when needed.

faqs.question: Which file types are supported?
faqs.answer: Common audio and video formats like MP3, WAV, M4A, AAC, FLAC, OGG, OPUS, MP4, MOV, MKV, WEBM, AVI, and M4V.

faqs.question: Can I use YouTube or SoundCloud links?
faqs.answer: Not right now. YouTube, SoundCloud, TikTok, and other webpage links are not supported. Upload the audio or video file, or paste a direct link to one.

faqs.question: Why is the first run slower?
faqs.answer: The speech model downloads the first time you run the tool. After that it is cached for faster use.

faqs.question: What does the output look like?
faqs.answer: You get a plain text transcript (.txt) that you can download or copy.
